sentences.zh: 唐有天下三百年，文章無慮三變。

translations.literal: The Tang possessed the realm for three hundred years; in literature there were roughly three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Over the three centuries that the Tang held the empire, literary style underwent no fewer than three major shifts.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗，大難始夷，沿江左餘風，絺句繪章，揣合低卬，故王、楊為之伯。

translations.literal: Under Gaozu and Taizong, when great calamities had just been pacified, they followed the surviving style of the Jiangzuo region, weaving sentences and painting chapters to fit rise and fall, therefore Wang and Yang became its leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu and Taizong, as the founding trials were only just settling, writers still followed the lingering southern style—embroidering lines and adorning passages to suit each occasion—so Wang Bo and Yang Su became the masters of the age.

sentences.zh: 玄宗好經術，群臣稍厭雕瑑，索理致，崇雅黜浮，氣益雄渾，則燕、許擅其宗。

translations.literal: Xuanzong loved classical learning; the ministers gradually grew weary of ornamental carving, sought principle and substance, honored elegance and dismissed frivolity, the tone grew ever more vigorous and ample, and then Yan and Xu monopolized its school.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong turned to classical studies, his courtiers grew weary of overwrought ornament; they sought meaning and substance, exalted refined dignity over shallow display, and the literary tone grew bolder and more majestic—until Zhang Yue and Xu Jingzong came to dominate the tradition.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐興已百年，諸儒爭自名家。

translations.literal: At this time the Tang rise had already been a hundred years, and the Confucian scholars each contended to establish their own schools.
translations.idiomatic: By then the dynasty had stood for a century, and scholars everywhere were striving to found schools in their own names.

sentences.zh: 大曆、正元間，美才輩出，擩嚌道真，涵泳聖涯，於是韓愈倡之，柳宗元、李翱、皇甫湜等和之，排逐百家，法度森嚴，抵轢晉、魏，上軋漢、周，唐之文完然為一王法，此其極也。

translations.literal: Between the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns, fine talents emerged in succession, chewing the truth of the Way and bathing in the sage's shore; then Han Yu initiated it, and Liu Zongyuan, Li Ao, Huangfu Shi, and others joined him, driving out the hundred schools, standards stern and strict, thrusting against Jin and Wei, pressing upward against Han and Zhou—Tang literature wholly became a single royal norm; this was its summit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali and Zhenyuan eras, brilliant writers appeared one after another, savoring the truth of the Way and steeping themselves in the sage's teaching. Han Yu took the lead, and Liu Zongyuan, Li Ao, Huangfu Shi, and others followed: they swept aside rival schools, enforced a rigorous style, rejected the manner of Jin and Wei, and reached back past them to Han and Zhou—until Tang prose stood complete as the dynasty's single authoritative standard. That was its zenith.

sentences.zh: 若侍從酬奉則李嶠、宋之問、沈佺期、王維，制冊則常袞、楊炎、陸贄、權德輿、王仲舒、李德裕，言詩則杜甫、李白、元稹、白居易、劉禹錫，譎怪則李賀、杜牧、李商隱，皆卓然以所長為一世冠，其可尚已。

translations.literal: For attendant court service and responses there were Li Jiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, and Wang Wei; for edicts and ordinances, Chang Gun, Yang Yan, Lu Zhi, Quan Deyu, Wang Zhongshu, and Li Deyu; for poetry, Du Fu, Li Bai, Yuan Zhen, Bai Juyi, and Liu Yuxi; for the strange and uncanny, Li He, Du Mu, and Li Shangyin—all outstanding, each making his specialty the crown of an age; how could they not be honored?
translations.idiomatic: For court verse and occasional pieces there were Li Jiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, and Wang Wei; for state documents, Chang Gun, Yang Yan, Lu Zhi, Quan Deyu, Wang Zhongshu, and Li Deyu; for poetry, Du Fu, Li Bai, Yuan Zhen, Bai Juyi, and Liu Yuxi; for the fantastic and grotesque, Li He, Du Mu, and Li Shangyin—each stood supreme in his own art for a generation. What more could one ask?

sentences.zh: 然嘗言之，夫子之門以文學為下科，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet it has been said: in the Master's gate, literary study was ranked as the lower course—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet it has often been asked: why did Confucius rank literary accomplishment among the lesser pursuits in his school?

sentences.zh: 蓋天之付與，于君子小人無常分，惟能者得之，故號一藝。

translations.literal: Heaven's gift has no fixed allotment between gentleman and petty man; only the capable obtain it, hence it is called a single art.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift bears no fixed label for noble or base; whoever has the talent may claim it, and so it is called a single art.

sentences.zh: 自中智以還，恃以取敗者有之，朋奸飾偽者有之，怨望訕國者有之。

translations.literal: From middling intelligence downward, some rely on it to court defeat; some band with villains to adorn falsehood; some harbor resentment and slander the state.
translations.idiomatic: Among men of merely average mind and below, some have leaned on it to bring ruin on themselves; some have joined with villains to dress up deceit; some have nursed grievance and mocked the realm.

sentences.zh: 若君子則不然，自能以功業行實光明于時，亦不一于立言而垂不腐，有如不得試，固且闡繹優遊，異不及排，怨不及誹，而不忘納君於善，故可貴也。

translations.literal: The gentleman is not so: he can by his own merit and conduct shine in his age, and does not rely solely on writing to endure uncorrupted; if he cannot be tried in office, he still expounds at leisure—strangeness does not reach exclusion, resentment does not reach slander—and he does not forget to lead his lord toward goodness; therefore he is precious.
translations.idiomatic: The true gentleman is otherwise: he lets deeds and conduct shine in his own time and does not depend on words alone to win immortality. Even when denied office, he still teaches at ease—never so eccentric as to invite rejection, never so bitter as to slander—and he never forgets to guide his ruler toward what is right. That is why such a man is worthy of honor.

sentences.zh: 今但取以文自名者為《文藝篇》，若韋應物、沈亞之、閻防、祖詠、薛能、鄭穀等，其類尚多，皆班班有文在人間，史家逸其行事，故弗得而述云。

translations.literal: Now we take only those who made a name by literature for the 'Literature and Arts' chapters; such as Wei Yingwu, Shen Yazhi, Yan Fang, Zu Yong, Xue Neng, Zheng Gu, and the like—there are still many of this kind, all clearly having writings among men; historians have omitted their conduct, and so we cannot narrate them.
translations.idiomatic: Here we include only those who won renown chiefly through letters in these 'Literature and Arts' chapters. Wei Yingwu, Shen Yazhi, Yan Fang, Zu Yong, Xue Neng, Zheng Gu, and many others like them all left distinguished writings in the world, but historians passed over their lives, and so we cannot recount them here.

sentences.zh: 袁朗袁朗，其先雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Yuan Lang—Yuan Lang's ancestors were natives of Chang'an in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lang was descended from a family of Chang'an in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 父樞，仕陳為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Shu served Chen as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu served the Chen as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朗在陳為秘書郎，江總尤器之。

translations.literal: Lang in Chen was a Secretary; Jiang Zong especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, Lang served as a secretary, and Jiang Zong held him in special esteem.

sentences.zh: 後主聞其才，詔為《月賦》一篇，灑然無留思，後主曰：「謝莊不得獨美於前矣。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler heard of his talent and ordered a 'Rhapsody on the Moon'; he composed it with flowing ease and no lingering effort. The Last Ruler said: 'Xie Zhuang can no longer monopolize the glory of former days.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen emperor heard of his gift, he ordered a rhapsody on the moon. Lang wrote it at a stroke, without hesitation. The emperor said, "Xie Zhuang will no longer have the field to himself."

sentences.zh: 」復詔為《芝草》、《嘉蓮》二頌，歎賞尤厚。

translations.literal: Again he was ordered to compose two hymns, 'Lingzhi Grass' and 'Fine Lotus,' and admiration was especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was then commissioned to write two hymns, on the auspicious fungus and the fine lotus, and the emperor's praise was lavish.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子洗馬、德教殿學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince's Attendant and Academician of the Hall of Virtuous Teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Crown Prince's Attendant and academician of the Hall of Virtuous Teaching.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，歷尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui and served as a Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, he entered Sui service and held a post in the Ceremonial Section of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武德初，隱太子與秦王、齊王相傾，爭致名臣以自助。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi opposed each other, each striving to win famous ministers to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, the Hidden Crown Prince, the Prince of Qin, and the Prince of Qi were locked in rivalry, each struggling to draw famous ministers to his side.

sentences.zh: 太子有詹事李綱、竇軌、庶子裴矩、鄭善果、友賀德仁、洗馬魏征、中舍人王珪、舍人徐師謨、率更令歐陽詢、典膳監任璨、直典書坊唐臨、隴西公府祭酒韋挺、記室參軍事庾抱、左領大都督府長史唐憲；

translations.literal: The Crown Prince had Chief Steward Li Gang, Dou Gui, Senior Tutor Pei Ju, Zheng Shanguo, Friend He Deren, Attendant Wei Zheng, Palace Attendant Wang Gui, Attendant Xu Shimou, Director of the Bureau of Astronomy Ouyang Xun, Director of Palace Provisions Ren Can, Directing Clerk of the Palace Library Tang Lin, Libationer of the Duke of Longxi's household Wei Ting, Recorder's Aide Yu Bao, and Chief Administrator of the Left Grand General's headquarters Tang Xian;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's circle included Chief Steward Li Gang, Dou Gui, Senior Tutor Pei Ju, Zheng Shanguo, Friend He Deren, Attendant Wei Zheng, Palace Attendant Wang Gui, Attendant Xu Shimou, Director of the Bureau of Astronomy Ouyang Xun, Director of Palace Provisions Ren Can, Directing Clerk of the Palace Library Tang Lin, Libationer of the Duke of Longxi's household Wei Ting, Recorder's Aide Yu Bao, and Chief Administrator of the Left Grand General's headquarters Tang Xian;

sentences.zh: 秦王有友于志甯、記室參軍事房玄齡、虞世南、顏思魯、諮議參軍事竇綸、蕭景、兵曹杜如晦、鎧曹褚遂良、士曹戴胄、閻立德、參軍事薛元敬、蔡允恭、主簿薛收、李道玄、典簽蘇幹、文學姚思廉、褚亮、敦煌公府文學顏師古、右元帥府司馬蕭瑀、行軍元帥府長史屈突通、司馬竇誕、天策府長史唐儉、司馬封倫、軍諮祭酒蘇世長、兵曹參軍事杜淹、倉曹李守素、參軍事顏相時；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin had Friend Yu Zhining, Recorder's Aides Fang Xuanling, Yu Shinan, Yan Silu, Advisory Aides Dou Lun and Xiao Jing, Military Registrar Du Ruhui, Armor Registrar Chu Suiliang, Personnel Registrar Dai Zhou, Yan Lide, Military Aides Xue Yuanjing, Cai Yungong, Chief Clerk Xue Shou, Li Daoxuan, Directing Clerk Su Gan, Literary Scholars Yao Silian and Chu Liang, Literary Scholar of the Duke of Dunhuang's household Yan Shigu, Right Marshal's Deputy Xiao Yu, Field Marshal's Chief Administrator Qu Tu Tong, Deputy Dou Yan, Heavenly Stratagem Chief Administrator Tang Jian, Deputy Feng Lun, Military Adviser Su Shichang, Military Aide Du Yan, Granary Registrar Li Shousu, and Military Aide Yan Xiangshi;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin had Friend Yu Zhining, Recorder's Aides Fang Xuanling, Yu Shinan, and Yan Silu, Advisory Aides Dou Lun and Xiao Jing, Military Registrar Du Ruhui, Armor Registrar Chu Suiliang, Personnel Registrar Dai Zhou, Yan Lide, Military Aides Xue Yuanjing, Cai Yungong, Chief Clerk Xue Shou, Li Daoxuan, Directing Clerk Su Gan, Literary Scholars Yao Silian and Chu Liang, Literary Scholar of the Duke of Dunhuang's household Yan Shigu, Right Marshal's Deputy Xiao Yu, Field Marshal's Chief Administrator Qu Tu Tong, Deputy Dou Yan, Heavenly Stratagem Chief Administrator Tang Jian, Deputy Feng Lun, Military Adviser Su Shichang, Military Aide Du Yan, Granary Registrar Li Shousu, and Military Aide Yan Xiangshi;

sentences.zh: 齊王有記室參軍事榮九思、戶曹武士逸、典簽裴宣儼，朗為文學。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi had Recorder's Aide Rong Jiusi, Household Registrar Wu Shiyi, Directing Clerk Pei Xuanyi, and Lang as Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi had Recorder's Aide Rong Jiusi, Household Registrar Wu Shiyi, Directing Clerk Pei Xuanyi, and Lang as literary scholar.

sentences.zh: 從父弟承序亦有名，王召為文學館學士。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Chengxu was also famous; the Prince summoned him as an Academician of the Literature Institute.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Chengxu was also well known, and the prince summoned him as an academician of the Literature Institute.

sentences.zh: 朗累封汝南縣男，再轉給事中。

translations.literal: Lang was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Runan County and was twice transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was enfeoffed as Baron of Runan County and later promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，太宗為廢朝一日，謂高士廉曰：「朗任淺而性謹厚，使人悼惜。

translations.literal: When he died, Taizong suspended court for one day and said to Gao Shilian: 'Lang's office was shallow but his nature careful and sincere—he makes one mourn.'
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Taizong suspended court for a day and told Gao Shilian, "Lang held only modest rank, yet his character was careful and sincere—a loss one cannot help mourning."

sentences.zh: 」詔給喪費，存問其家。

translations.literal: An edict granted funeral expenses and sent condolences to his family.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted funeral expenses and sent condolences to his family.

sentences.zh: 朗遠祖滂，為漢司徒。

translations.literal: Lang's remote ancestor Pang was Han Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's distant ancestor Pang had served the Han as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 自滂至朗凡十二世，其間位司徒、司空者四世，淑、顗、察皆死宋難，昂著節齊、梁。

translations.literal: From Pang to Lang were twelve generations in all; among them four generations held the posts of Minister over the Masses or Minister of Works; Shu, Yan, and Cha all died in Song's calamity; Ang showed integrity in Qi and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: From Pang to Lang stretched twelve generations; four of them had held the rank of Minister over the Masses or Minister of Works. Shu, Yan, and Cha all perished in the troubles of Song; Ang won renown for constancy under Qi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 時朗自以中外人物為海內冠，雖琅邪王氏踵為公卿，特以累朝佐命有功，鄙不為伍。

translations.literal: At the time Lang considered his family's men within and without the court the foremost in the realm; though the Wang clan of Langye in succession became high ministers, he scorned to rank with them, holding that they owed their place only to assisting successive founders.
translations.idiomatic: Lang regarded his own clan, inside and outside office, as the foremost in the land. Though the Wangs of Langye had filled one high post after another, he disdained their company, saying they owed their standing only to helping successive dynasties seize power.

sentences.zh: 孫 誼朗孫誼，神功中為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandson Yi—Lang's grandson Yi, during the Shenggong era was Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yi served as prefect of Suzhou during the Shenggong reign.

sentences.zh: 司馬張沛者，侍中文瓘子，嘗白誼曰：「州得一長史，隴西李亶，天下甲門也。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhang Pei, son of Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Jin, once told Yi: 'The prefecture has gained a Chief Administrator, Li Dan of Longxi—a foremost clan under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: His assistant administrator Zhang Pei, son of the attendant Zhang Jin, once told Yi, "We have a new chief administrator—Li Dan of Longxi, from one of the empire's greatest houses."

sentences.zh: 」誼曰：「夫門戶者，曆世名節為天下所高，老夫是也。

translations.literal: Yi said: 'As for a great house, it is one whose fame and integrity through generations are honored by the realm—that is what I am.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "A great house is one whose fame and integrity have been honored for generations—that is what my family is."

sentences.zh: 山東人尚婚媾，求祿利耳，至見危受命，則無人焉，何足尚邪？

translations.literal: Men east of the mountains value marriage alliances and seek salary and profit; when it comes to accepting office in peril, there is no one—how can they be honored?
translations.idiomatic: Men east of the mountains care for marriage ties and profit; when danger comes and duty calls, not one of them steps forward. What is there to admire?"

sentences.zh: 」沛大慚。

translations.literal: Pei was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 從父弟 承序承序為齊王元吉府學士，府廢，補建昌令。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Chengxu—Chengxu was an academician in Prince Yuanji of Qi's princely household; when the household was abolished he was appointed Magistrate of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Chengxu had been an academician in Prince Yuanji of Qi's household. When that household was abolished, he was appointed magistrate of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 治尚慈簡，吏民懷德。

translations.literal: His governance favored kindness and simplicity; officials and people cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with kindness and simplicity, and officials and common people alike cherished him.

sentences.zh: 高宗之為晉王也，太宗崇選僚屬，問梁、陳名臣子弟誰可者。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was Prince of Jin, Taizong greatly valued choosing staff and asked who among the sons of famous ministers of Liang and Chen would do.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was still Prince of Jin, Taizong took great care in choosing his staff and asked which sons of famous Liang and Chen ministers would be suitable.

sentences.zh: 岑文本曰：「昔陳亡，百司奔散，有袁憲者，朝服立後主傍，白刃不避也。

translations.literal: Cen Textian said: 'When Chen fell, the hundred offices scattered in flight; yet Yuan Xian stood in court dress beside the Last Ruler and did not avoid naked blades.'
translations.idiomatic: Cen Textian said, "When Chen fell, the bureaucracy fled in panic, yet Yuan Xian stood in court dress beside the last emperor and did not flinch from drawn swords."

sentences.zh: 王世充篡隋，群臣表勸進，而憲子給事中承家稱疾不肯署。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped Sui, the ministers submitted memorials urging accession, but Xian's son Palace Attendant Chengjia pleaded illness and refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong seized Sui, the ministers urged him to take the throne, but Xian's son Chengjia, a palace attendant, pleaded illness and refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 今其少子承序，風操清亮，無愧先烈。

translations.literal: Now his youngest son Chengxu—bearing and conduct clear and bright—does not disgrace his forebears.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chengxu now bears himself with the same clear integrity and is worthy of his ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃召拜晉王友、兼侍讀，加弘文館學士，卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor then summoned and appointed him Friend of the Prince of Jin, concurrently Reader, and added him as Academician of the Hongwen Institute; he later died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed him friend to the Prince of Jin and concurrent reader, and made him an academician of the Hongwen Institute. He later died in office.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟 利貞朗從祖弟利貞，陳中書令敬孫，高宗時為太常博士、周王侍讀。

translations.literal: Cousin Lizhen—Lang's cousin Lizhen, grandson of Chen's Director of the Imperial Secretariat Jing, in Gaozong's time was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Reader to the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lizhen, grandson of the Chen director Jing, served under Gaozong as an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and reader to the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及王立為太子，百官上禮，帝欲大會群臣、命婦合宴宣政殿，設九部伎、散樂。

translations.literal: When the prince was established as Crown Prince, the hundred officials presented congratulations; the Emperor wished to hold a great assembly of ministers and titled ladies for a joint banquet in the Hall of Proclaiming Government, setting up the nine orchestras and miscellaneous music.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was made heir, the officials offered congratulations, and the emperor planned a grand banquet in the Hall of Proclaiming Government for ministers and titled ladies together, with the nine orchestras and popular entertainments.

sentences.zh: 利貞上疏諫，以為：「前殿路門，非命婦宴會、倡優進御之所，請徙命婦別殿，九部伎從左右門入，罷散樂不進。

translations.literal: Lizhen submitted a memorial remonstrating, holding that: 'The front hall and Road Gate are not places for titled ladies' banquets or for actors and singers to enter the imperial presence; I beg that titled ladies be moved to a separate hall, the nine orchestras enter through the left and right gates, and miscellaneous music be stopped and not brought in.'
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen remonstrated in a memorial: "The front hall and its main gate are not fit for banquets of titled ladies or for actors and singers before the throne. I ask that the ladies feast in another hall, that the nine orchestras enter by the side gates, and that popular entertainments be omitted entirely."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 既會，帝傳詔利貞曰：「卿奕葉忠鯁，能抗疏規朕之失，不厚賜無以勸能者。

translations.literal: After the assembly, the Emperor sent word to Lizhen: 'You through generations have been loyal and upright; you could submit a memorial against my fault—without generous reward there is no way to encourage the capable.'
translations.idiomatic: After the feast, the emperor sent word to Lizhen: "Your family has been loyal for generations, and you dared remonstrate with me. Without a generous reward I could not encourage such men."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜物百段。

translations.literal: He then bestowed a hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him a hundred rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 擢祠部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Rites and later died.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，以舊恩追贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was established, in recognition of old favor he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong came to the throne, he was posthumously made vice director of the Imperial Library in recognition of past service.

sentences.zh: 賀德仁賀德仁，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: He Deren—He Deren was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Deren was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父朗，終陳散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Lang ended as Chen's Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lang had ended his career as a regular attendant under Chen.

sentences.zh: 德仁與從兄德基師事周弘正，以文辭稱，人為語曰：「學行可師賀德基，文質彬彬賀德仁。

translations.literal: Deren and his cousin Deji studied under Zhou Hongzheng and were famed for literary composition; people made a saying: 'In learning and conduct one may take He Deji as teacher; in literary grace and substance, He Deren is refined.'
translations.idiomatic: Deren and his cousin Deji studied under Zhou Hongzheng and won fame for their writing. People said, "Take He Deji as your model in learning and conduct; in literary grace and substance, none surpasses He Deren."

sentences.zh: 」兄弟八人，時比漢荀氏，太守鄱陽王伯山改所居甘滂里為高陽云。

translations.literal: Eight brothers in all—at the time compared to the Xun clan of Han; the Prefect, Prince of Poyang Wang Boshan, changed their residence's Ganpang Lane to Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The eight brothers were compared in their day to the Xuns of Han, and the prefect, Prince Boshan of Poyang, renamed their lane from Ganpang to Gaoyang in their honor.

sentences.zh: 始，德仁在陳，為吳興王友。

translations.literal: At first Deren in Chen was Friend to the Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, Deren first served as friend to the Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 入隋，楊素薦其材，授豫章王記室，王遇之厚；

translations.literal: Entering Sui, Yang Su recommended his talent; he was appointed Recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang, and the prince treated him generously;
translations.idiomatic: After Sui was founded, Yang Su recommended him, and he was made recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang, who treated him with great favor;

sentences.zh: 徙封齊，復為府屬。

translations.literal: when the prince was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, he again became a household officer.
translations.idiomatic: when the prince was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, he again became a member of his household staff.

sentences.zh: 王廢，官吏抵罪，而德仁以忠謹獲貰，補河東司法參軍。

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed, officials were punished, but Deren through loyalty and prudence was pardoned and appointed Military Assistant in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was deposed, his staff were punished, but Deren was pardoned for loyalty and care and was appointed military assistant in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 素與隱太子善，高祖起兵，太子封隴西公，以德仁為友，庾抱為記室。

translations.literal: Su was on good terms with the Hidden Crown Prince; when Gaozu raised troops, the Crown Prince was enfeoffed Duke of Longxi, with Deren as Friend and Yu Bao as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Su was close to the Hidden Crown Prince. When Gaozu raised his army, the prince was made Duke of Longxi, with Deren as friend and Yu Bao as recorder.

sentences.zh: 俄並遷中舍人。

translations.literal: Soon both were transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both were promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 以年耆不更吏職，徙洗馬，與蕭德言、陳子良皆為東宮學士。

translations.literal: Because of advanced age he no longer held administrative office and was moved to Attendant, and with Xiao Deyan and Chen Ziliang all became Eastern Palace Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age he left regular office and became crown prince's attendant; he, Xiao Deyan, and Chen Ziliang all served as Eastern Palace academicians.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷趙王友，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to Friend of the Prince of Zhao and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was made friend to the Prince of Zhao and died in office.

sentences.zh: 從子紀、敱亦博學。

translations.literal: His nephews Ji and Ai were also broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Ji and Ai were also widely learned.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，紀為太子洗馬，豫修五禮，敱率更令、兼太子侍讀，皆為崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time Ji was Crown Prince's Attendant and took part in compiling the Five Rites; Ai was Director of the Bureau of Astronomy and concurrently Crown Prince's Reader—both were Academicians of the Hall of Esteeming Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Ji served as crown prince's attendant and helped compile the Five Rites; Ai was director of the Bureau of Astronomy and concurrent reader to the crown prince. Both were academicians of the Hall of Esteeming Worthies.

sentences.zh: 附 庾抱抱者，陳御史中丞眾孫。

translations.literal: Appended: Yu Bao—Bao was grandson of Chen's Censor-in-Chief Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Yu Bao was grandson of the Chen censor-in-chief Zhong.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為延州參軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he was Military Assistant in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he served as military assistant in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入調吏部，尚書牛弘給筆劄，令自序，援筆而成。

translations.literal: Entering for evaluation at the Ministry of Personnel, Director Niu Hong gave him brush and paper and ordered a self-account; he took up the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported to the Ministry of Personnel, Director Niu Hong gave him brush and paper and asked for a self-account; he wrote it at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 為元德太子學士，會嫡皇孫生，大宴，坐中獻頌，太子嗟賞。

translations.literal: He was Academician to the Yuande Crown Prince; when the legitimate imperial grandson was born, there was a great banquet, and seated he presented a hymn—the Crown Prince sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He became academician to Crown Prince Yuande. When the legitimate imperial grandson was born, a great banquet was held; Bao presented a hymn from his seat, and the crown prince praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 及在隴西府，文檄皆出其手。

translations.literal: When he was in the Duke of Longxi's household, all documents and proclamations came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the Duke of Longxi's household, all documents and proclamations came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 蔡允恭蔡允恭，荊州江陵人，後樑左民尚書大業子。

translations.literal: Cai Yungong—Cai Yungong was a native of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture, son of Later Liang's Minister of the Left Household Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yungong was a native of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture and son of Daye, minister of the left household under Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，工為詩。

translations.literal: Handsome in appearance, skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，曆起居舍人。

translations.literal: He served Sui and held the post of Attendant of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: He served Sui and rose to attendant of the diary of activity and repose.

sentences.zh: 煬帝有所賦，必令諷誦。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Yang composed something, he always ordered Yungong to recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Yang wrote a new poem, he had Yungong recite it aloud.

sentences.zh: 遣教宮人，允恭恥之，數稱疾。

translations.literal: He was sent to instruct palace women; Yungong was ashamed of this and repeatedly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ordered to teach palace women, Yungong was ashamed and repeatedly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 授內史舍人，俾入宮，因辭，繇是疏斥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and ordered to enter the palace; he declined, and thereby was estranged and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant of the Palace Secretariat and ordered into the palace; he refused, and from then on fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 帝遇弑，經事宇文化及、竇建德，歸國為秦王府參軍、文學館學士。

translations.literal: When the Emperor met assassination, he passed through service under Yuwen Huaji and Dou Jiande; returning to the realm he became Military Aide in the Prince of Qin's household and Academician of the Literature Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was killed, he served Yuwen Huaji and Dou Jiande in turn; when he returned to Tang he became military aide in the Prince of Qin's household and academician of the Literature Institute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，除太子洗馬，卒，著《後樑春秋》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Crown Prince's Attendant and died; he authored the 'Spring and Autumn of Later Liang.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was made crown prince's attendant and died; he wrote the Spring and Autumn of Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 謝偃謝偃，衛州衛人，本姓直勒氏，祖孝政，仕北齊為散騎常侍，改姓謝。

translations.literal: Xie Yan—Xie Yan was a native of Wei in Wei Prefecture; his original surname was the Zhile clan; his grandfather Xiaozheng served Northern Qi as Regular Attendant and changed the surname to Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan was a native of Wei in Wei Prefecture. His family had borne the surname Zhile; his grandfather Xiaozheng served Northern Qi as regular attendant and took the surname Xie.

sentences.zh: 偃在隋為散從正員郎。

translations.literal: Yan in Sui was a Regular Gentleman of the Scattered Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, Yan held the rank of regular gentleman of the scattered retinue.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，應詔對策高第，曆高陵主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he answered the imperial examination with high rank and served as Chief Clerk of Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he passed the imperial examination with high honors and served as chief clerk of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸東都，方穀、洛壞洛陽宮，詔求直言，偃上書陳得失，帝稱善，引為弘文館直學士，遷魏王府功曹。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited the Eastern Capital, the Gu and Luo rivers were damaging Luoyang Palace; an edict sought forthright speech. Yan submitted a memorial stating gains and losses; the Emperor praised it and summoned him as Direct Academician of the Hongwen Institute, then transferred him to Merit Officer in the Prince of Wei's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong visited the eastern capital, the Gu and Luo rivers were damaging Luoyang Palace, and he called for frank counsel. Yan submitted a memorial on the empire's strengths and faults; the emperor praised it, made him a direct academician of the Hongwen Institute, and later transferred him to merit officer in the Prince of Wei's household.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《塵》、《影賦》二篇，帝美其文，召見，欲偃作賦。

translations.literal: He once composed two rhapsodies, 'Dust' and 'Shadow'; the Emperor admired his writing, summoned him, and wished Yan to compose a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote two rhapsodies, Dust and Shadow. The emperor admired them, summoned him, and asked for another.

sentences.zh: 先為序一篇，頗言天下乂安、功德茂盛意，授偃使賦。

translations.literal: First he composed a preface stating at length the idea that the realm was at peace and merit abundant, and entrusted Yan to write the rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first wrote a preface celebrating the realm's peace and abundant merit, then commissioned Yan to write the rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 偃緣帝指，名篇曰《述聖》，帝悅，賜帛數十。

translations.literal: Yan followed the Emperor's intent and named the piece 'Narrating the Sage'; the Emperor was pleased and bestowed several tens of bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yan followed the emperor's theme and titled the piece Narrating the Sage. The emperor was pleased and granted him several dozen bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位，直中書省張蘊古上《大寶箴》，諷帝以民畏而未懷，其辭挺切，擢大理丞。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor took the throne, Zhang Yungu of the Direct Service in the Palace Secretariat submitted the 'Great Treasure Admonition,' admonishing the Emperor that the people feared but did not cherish him; the language was stern and cutting, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, Zhang Yungu of the Palace Secretariat submitted the Great Treasure Admonition, warning that the people feared him but did not love him. Its language was sharp, and he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 偃又獻《惟皇誠德賦》，其序大略言：「治忘亂，安忘危，逸忘勞，得忘失，四者人主莫不然。

translations.literal: Yan also presented the 'Rhapsody on the Emperor's Sincere Virtue'; its preface stated in outline: 'In order one forgets disorder; in security one forgets peril; in ease one forgets toil; in gain one forgets loss—these four, no ruler fails to do so.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan also presented the Rhapsody on the Emperor's Sincere Virtue. Its preface said in essence: "In peace rulers forget chaos; in safety they forget danger; in ease they forget labor; in possession they forget loss—no sovereign escapes these four."

sentences.zh: 桀以瑤台為麗，而不悟南巢之禍；

translations.literal: Jie took the Jade Terrace as splendor and did not perceive the calamity of Nanchao;
translations.idiomatic: Jie took pride in his Jade Terrace and did not foresee the disaster at Nanchao;

sentences.zh: 殷辛以象箸為華，而不知牧野之敗。

translations.literal: Yin Xin took ivory chopsticks as glory and did not know the defeat at Muye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou took ivory chopsticks for glory and did not foresee defeat at Muye.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人處宮室則思前王所以亡，朝萬國則思己所以尊，巡府庫則思今所以得，視功臣則思其輔佐之始，見名將則思用力之初，如此則人無易心，天下何患乎不化哉？

translations.literal: Therefore the sage, when dwelling in palaces, thinks how former kings perished; when holding court for the ten thousand states, thinks how he himself came to honor; when touring treasuries, thinks how he now came to obtain them; when viewing meritorious ministers, thinks how they first aided him; when seeing famous generals, thinks how they first exerted strength—if so, people will have no change of heart; what worry is there that the realm will not be transformed?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage, in his palace, recalls how earlier kings fell; in audience with the realm, recalls how he won honor; in the treasury, recalls how he came by his wealth; before his ministers, recalls how they first served him; before his generals, recalls how they first fought for him. Then the people's hearts will not waver—what fear is there that the realm will not be transformed?

sentences.zh: 旦行之堯、舜，暮失之桀、紂，豈異人哉？

translations.literal: Acting as Yao and Shun in the morning, losing it as Jie and Zhou in the evening—are they different men?
translations.idiomatic: The same man may act as Yao and Shun in the morning and fall like Jie and Zhou by evening—are they different people?

sentences.zh: 」其賦蓋規帝成功而自處至難云。

translations.literal: His rhapsody was essentially admonishing the Emperor that after success, placing oneself was most difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsody itself warned the emperor that after success, holding one's position is hardest of all.

sentences.zh: 又撰《玉諜真紀》以勸封禪。

translations.literal: He also compiled the 'True Record of the Jade Chart' to urge the Feng and Shan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the True Record of the Jade Chart to urge the emperor to perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時李百藥工詩，而偃善賦，時人稱「李詩謝賦」。

translations.literal: At the time Li Baiyao was skilled in poetry while Yan was skilled in rhapsody; contemporaries called them 'Li's poetry, Xie's rhapsody.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Baiyao excelled in poetry and Yan in rhapsody, and people spoke of "Li's poems and Xie's rhapsodies."

sentences.zh: 府廢，終湘潭令。

translations.literal: When the princely household was abolished, he ended as Magistrate of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's household was abolished, he ended his career as magistrate of Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 蘊古，洹水人。

translations.literal: Yungu was a native of Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yungu was a native of Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 敏書傳，曉世務，文擅當時。

translations.literal: Quick in the classics, versed in affairs of the age, his writing dominated the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick in the classics, versed in affairs of state, and his writing stood foremost in his day.

sentences.zh: 後坐事誅。

translations.literal: Later he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 崔信明崔信明，青州益都人。

translations.literal: Cui Xinming—Cui Xinming was a native of Yidu in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinming was a native of Yidu in Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖光伯，仕後魏為七兵尚書。

translations.literal: His ancestor Guangbo served Later Wei as Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Guangbo had served Later Wei as Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 信明之生，五月五日日方中，有異雀鳴集庭樹，太史令史良為占曰：「五月為火，火主《離》，《離》為文，日中，文之盛也，雀五色而鳴，此兒將以文顯。

translations.literal: When Xinming was born, on the fifth day of the fifth month the sun was at its zenith; a strange bird cried and gathered in the courtyard tree. Grand Astrologer Clerk Shi Liang divined, saying: 'The fifth month is fire; fire governs Li; Li is literature; at midday is literature's fullness; the bird is five-colored and cries—this child will be illustrious through literature.'
translations.idiomatic: Xinming was born at noon on the fifth day of the fifth month. A strange bird cried in the courtyard tree. The grand astrologer's clerk Shi Liang divined: "The fifth month belongs to fire; fire governs the hexagram Li, which stands for writing; noon is writing at its height; a five-colored bird cries—this child will win fame through letters."

sentences.zh: 然雀類微，位殆不高邪。

translations.literal: Yet the bird's kind is slight—his rank will perhaps not be high.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bird is a humble creature—his office may not rise very high."

sentences.zh: 」及長，強記，美文章。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he had a powerful memory and fine literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he had a prodigious memory and wrote fine prose and verse.

sentences.zh: 鄉人高孝基嘗語人曰：「崔生才富，為一時冠，但恨位不到耳。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Gao Xiaoji once said to people: 'Young Cui's talent is abundant—he is the crown of the age—but it is a pity his rank does not match.'
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman, Gao Xiaoji, once said, "Young Cui's talent is abundant—he stands foremost in his generation—but it is a pity his rank does not match."

sentences.zh: 」隋大業中，為堯城令。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was Magistrate of Yaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Daye reign he served as magistrate of Yaocheng.

sentences.zh: 竇建德僭號，而信明族弟敬素者，為賊鴻臚卿，自謂得意，語信明曰：「夏王英武，有舉天下心，士女繈負而至不可數。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande usurped the title, and Xinming's clansman Jingsu served the rebel as Director of Ceremonies, deeming himself successful; he said to Xinming: 'The King of Xia is heroic and martial, with the heart to raise the realm; men and women come carrying children on their backs, beyond counting.'
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande seized power, Xinming's kinsman Jingsu became the rebel director of ceremonies and, flushed with success, told Xinming, "The King of Xia is heroic and aims to take the realm. Men and women are flocking to him with children on their backs beyond count."

sentences.zh: 兄不以此時立功立事，豈所謂見幾不俟終日乎？

translations.literal: Brother, if you do not at this time establish merit and achievement, is this what is called seeing the moment and not waiting even a day?
translations.idiomatic: Brother, if you do not seize this moment to win merit, what becomes of the saying that one who sees the turn of fortune does not wait even a day?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔申胥海隅釣師，能固其節。

translations.literal: He replied: 'In former days Shen Xu was a fishing master at the sea's edge, yet could hold fast to his integrity.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Long ago Shen Xu was only a fisherman by the sea, yet he held fast to his integrity."

sentences.zh: 爾欲吾屈身賊中求斗筲邪？

translations.literal: Do you wish me to bend my body among rebels seeking a pittance?
translations.idiomatic: Do you want me to bow to rebels for a petty post?"

sentences.zh: 」遂逾城去，隱太行山。

translations.literal: He then crossed the wall and left, hiding on Mount Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled over the city wall and hid on Mount Taihang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，有詔即家拜興勢丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan an edict appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Xingshi at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan an edict appointed him assistant magistrate of Xingshi without requiring him to leave home.

sentences.zh: 遷秦川令，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Qinchuan and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made magistrate of Qinchuan and died in office.

sentences.zh: 信明蹇亢，以門望自負，嘗矜其文，謂過李百藥，議者不許。

translations.literal: Xinming was proud and unyielding, taking pride in his family's standing; he once boasted of his writing, saying it surpassed Li Baiyao, but critics did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming was proud and difficult, swaggering on his family's standing. He once boasted that his writing surpassed Li Baiyao's, but critics would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 揚州錄事參軍鄭世翼者，亦驁倨，數恌輕忤物，遇信明江中，謂曰：「聞公有'楓落吳江冷'，願見其餘。

translations.literal: Zheng Shiyi, Military Assistant Recorder of Yang Prefecture, was also arrogant and haughty, often rashly slighting and offending others; meeting Xinming on the river, he said: 'I have heard your line "Maples fall, the Wu River cold"—I wish to see the rest.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shiyi, recorder of Yang Prefecture, was equally arrogant and often gave offense. Meeting Xinming on the river, he said, "I have heard your line about maples falling and the Wu River cold—I should like to see the rest."

sentences.zh: 」信明欣然多出眾篇，世翼覽未終，曰：「所見不逮所聞！

translations.literal: Xinming gladly produced many of his best pieces; Shiyi had not finished reading when he said: 'What is seen does not match what is heard!'
translations.idiomatic: Xinming gladly brought out many of his best pieces. Before Shiyi had finished reading, he said, "What I see does not match what I have heard!"

sentences.zh: 」投諸水，引舟去。

translations.literal: He threw them into the water and poled his boat away.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the poems into the water and poled his boat away.

sentences.zh: 附 鄭世翼世翼，鄭州滎陽人，周儀同大將軍敬德孫。

translations.literal: Appended: Zheng Shiyi—Shiyi was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture, grandson of Zhou's General of Equal Rank Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zheng Shiyi was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture and grandson of the Zhou general Jingde.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，坐怨謗流死巂州。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, for resentful slander he was exiled and died in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he was exiled for slander and died in Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 撰《交遊傳》，行於世。

translations.literal: He authored the 'Biographies of Friends,' which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Biographies of Friends, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 信明子冬日，武后時位黃門侍郎，為酷吏誣死。

translations.literal: Xinming's son Dongri, in Empress Wu's time held the post of Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and was falsely accused and killed by a cruel official.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming's son Dongri served under Empress Wu as vice director of the Yellow Gate and was framed and killed by a cruel official.

sentences.zh: 劉延祐劉延祐，徐州彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Yanyou—Liu Yanyou was a native of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanyou was a native of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯父胤之，少志學，與孫萬壽、李百藥相友善。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Yinzi, from youth intent on learning, was on friendly terms with Sun Wanshou and Li Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yinzi had studied earnestly from youth and was close friends with Sun Wanshou and Li Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 武德中，杜淹薦為信都令，有惠政。

translations.literal: In Wude, Du Yan recommended him as Magistrate of Xindu; he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, Du Yan recommended him as magistrate of Xindu, where his rule was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，以著作郎、弘文館學士與令狐德棻、陽仁卿等撰次國史並實錄，以勞封陽城縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, as Author and Academician of the Hongwen Institute he joined Linghu Defen, Yang Renqing, and others in compiling the national history and veritable records; for his labor he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he served as author and Hongwen academician, and with Linghu Defen, Yang Renqing, and others compiled the national history and veritable records. For this service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 終楚州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 延祐擢進士，補渭南尉，有吏能，治第一。

translations.literal: Yanyou passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Weinan, had administrative ability, and his governance ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan. He proved an able administrator, and his district ranked first.

sentences.zh: 李勣戒之曰：「子春秋少而有美名，宜稍自抑，無為出人上。

translations.literal: Li Jiji admonished him: 'You are still young in years yet already have a fine reputation; you should restrain yourself somewhat and not stand above others.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji warned him, "You are still young and already famous. You should hold yourself back a little and not rise above others."

sentences.zh: 」延祐欽納。

translations.literal: Yanyou respectfully accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 後檢校司賓少卿，封薛縣男。

translations.literal: Later he was made Acting Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies and enfeoffed Baron of Xue County.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made acting vice director of the Court for Dependencies and enfeoffed as Baron of Xue County.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業敗，詔延祐持節到軍。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye was defeated, an edict ordered Yanyou to proceed to the army bearing credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye was defeated, an edict sent Yanyou to the army with imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 時吏議敬業所署五品官殊死，六品流，延祐謂誣脅可察以情，乃論授五品官當流，六品以下除名，全宥甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time officials proposed that fifth-rank officers appointed by Jingye receive death, and sixth-rank exile; Yanyou held that those coerced by false accusation could be judged by circumstance, and argued that fifth-rank appointees should be exiled, sixth-rank and below dismissed from office—many were wholly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then proposed death for fifth-rank appointees of Jingye's and exile for sixth-rank men. Yanyou argued that many had been coerced and should be judged by circumstance: fifth-rank men should be exiled, sixth-rank and below dismissed, and a great many were wholly spared.

sentences.zh: 拜箕州刺史，轉安南都護。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Jizhou and transferred to Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jizhou and later transferred to protector-general of Annan.

sentences.zh: 舊俚戶歲半租，延祐責全入，眾始怨，謀亂。

translations.literal: Formerly the Liao households paid half rent yearly; Yanyou demanded full payment, and the people first grew resentful and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The indigenous households had long paid only half the annual rent, but Yanyou demanded full payment. Resentment spread and rebellion was plotted.

sentences.zh: 延祐誅其渠李嗣仙，而餘黨丁建等遂叛，合眾圍安南府。

translations.literal: Yanyou executed their leader Li Sixian, but the remaining faction Ding Jian and others then rebelled, gathering forces to besiege the Annan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou executed their leader Li Sixian, but the rest, led by Ding Jian, rose in revolt and besieged the Annan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少不支，嬰壘待援。

translations.literal: Troops in the city were few and could not hold; they closed the ramparts and awaited relief.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was too small to hold the city; they closed the walls and waited for relief.

sentences.zh: 廣州大族馮子猷幸立功，按兵不出，延祐遇害。

translations.literal: Feng Ziyou of the great Guangzhou clan, hoping to win merit, held his troops and did not advance; Yanyou met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ziyou, a great Guangzhou magnate hoping to win merit for himself, held back his troops and did not advance. Yanyou was killed.

sentences.zh: 桂州司馬曹玄靜進兵討建，斬之。

translations.literal: Gui Prefecture's Military Assistant Cao Xuanjing advanced troops to attack Jian and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xuanjing, military assistant of Gui Prefecture, marched against Jian and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 從弟 藏器延祐從弟藏器，高宗時為侍御史。

translations.literal: Cousin Zangqi—Yanyou's cousin Zangqi, in Gaozong's time was Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou's cousin Zangqi served under Gaozong as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 衛尉卿尉遲寶琳脅人為妾，藏器劾還之，寶琳私請帝止其還，凡再劾再止。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Yuchi Baolin coerced a woman into being his concubine; Zangqi impeached and had her returned; Baolin privately asked the Emperor to stop the return—twice impeached, twice stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Yuchi Baolin had forced a woman to become his concubine. Zangqi impeached him and ordered her returned. Baolin privately asked the emperor to block the order, and twice the emperor halted Zangqi's ruling.

sentences.zh: 藏器曰：「法為天下縣衡，萬民所共，陛下用舍繇情，法何所施？

translations.literal: Zangqi said: 'Law is the scale of the realm, shared by the myriad people; if Your Majesty grants or withholds according to personal feeling, how can law be applied?'
translations.idiomatic: Zangqi said, "Law is the scale of the realm, shared by all the people. If Your Majesty grants or withholds according to personal feeling, how can law be applied?"

sentences.zh: 今寶琳私請，陛下從之；

translations.literal: Now Baolin makes a private request and Your Majesty follows it;
translations.idiomatic: Now Baolin makes a private request and Your Majesty grants it;

sentences.zh: 臣公劾，陛下亦從之。

translations.literal: when your servant impeaches publicly, Your Majesty also follows it.
translations.idiomatic: when your servant impeaches in public, Your Majesty also grants it.

sentences.zh: 今日從，明日改，下何所遵？

translations.literal: Today you follow, tomorrow you change—what will those below follow?
translations.idiomatic: Today you grant, tomorrow you revoke—what are those below to follow?"

sentences.zh: 彼匹夫匹婦猶憚失信，況天子乎！

translations.literal: Even common men and women fear breaking faith—how much more the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Even common men and women fear to break faith—how much more the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃詔可，然內銜之，不悅也。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued an edict approving, yet inwardly harbored resentment and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then approved by edict, but inwardly resented him and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 稍遷比部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 監察御史魏元忠稱其賢，帝欲擢任為吏部侍郎，魏玄同沮曰：「彼守道不篤者，安用之？

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wei Yuanzhong praised his worth; the Emperor wished to promote him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, but Wei Xuantong dissuaded him, saying: 'He is one who does not hold firmly to the Way—how can he be used?'
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Wei Yuanzhong praised his worth, and the emperor wished to make him vice director of the Ministry of Personnel. Wei Xuantong dissuaded him, saying, "He does not hold firmly to the Way—of what use is he?"

sentences.zh: 」遂出為宋州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as Military Assistant of Song Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military assistant of Song Prefecture and died there.

sentences.zh: 子 知柔子知柔，性簡靜，美風儀。

translations.literal: Son Zhirou—Zhirou was by nature simple and quiet, with fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhirou was by nature quiet and restrained, with a fine bearing.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，廬墓側，詔築闕表之。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parent he built a hut beside the tomb; an edict ordered a memorial gate erected to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he built a hut beside the tomb, and an edict ordered a memorial gate erected in his honor.

sentences.zh: 曆國子司業，累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the Directorate of Education and rose to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，河南大水，詔知柔馳驛察民疾苦及吏善惡，所表陳州刺史韋嗣立、汝州刺史崔日用、兗州刺史韋元珪、符離令綦毋頊等，止二十七人有治狀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, Henan suffered great flood; an edict ordered Zhirou to travel by post-horse and inspect the people's suffering and officials' good and evil; among those he memorialized—Prefect of Chen Wei Sili, Prefect of Ru Cui Riyong, Prefect of Yan Wei Yuangui, Magistrate of Fuli Qimu Xu, and others—only twenty-seven had records of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, Henan suffered a great flood, and Zhirou was ordered to travel post-haste and inspect the people's suffering and officials' conduct. Of those he reported—including the prefects Wei Sili, Cui Riyong, and Wei Yuangui and the magistrate Qimu Xu—only twenty-seven had records of good governance.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷太子賓客，封彭城縣侯。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed Marquis of Pengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made mentor to the heir apparent and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 致仕，給全祿終身。

translations.literal: He retired and was granted full salary for life.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and was granted his full salary for life.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，祖載服用皆自處其費。

translations.literal: His final instructions ordered a simple burial; the funeral procession and garments were all paid from his own means.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions for a simple burial and paid all funeral expenses himself.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior mentor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 弟知幾，別有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhiji has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhiji has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 張昌齡張昌齡，冀州南宮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Changling—Zhang Changling was a native of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changling was a native of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與兄昌宗皆以文自名，州欲舉秀才，昌齡以科廢久，固讓。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Changzong both made a name through literature; the prefecture wished to recommend him as xiucai, but Changling, because the category had long been abolished, firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Changzong both won renown through letters. When the prefecture wished to recommend him as xiucai, Changling firmly declined, noting that the category had long been abolished.

sentences.zh: 更舉進士，與王公治齊名，皆為考功員外郎王師旦所絀。

translations.literal: He was instead recommended for jinshi; he and Wang Gongzhi were equally famous, and both were failed by Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Shidan.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead entered for the jinshi examination. He and Wang Gongzhi were equally famous, and both were failed by Wang Shidan of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太宗問其故，答曰：「昌齡等華而少實，其文浮靡，非令器也。

translations.literal: Taizong asked the reason; he replied: 'Changling and the others are florid and lacking substance; their writing is frivolous and ornate—not fit material.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked why. He replied, "Changling and the others are showy and shallow; their writing is frivolous and ornate—not fit material."

sentences.zh: 取之則後生勸慕，亂陛下風雅。

translations.literal: If they are taken, later students will be encouraged to emulate and will disorder Your Majesty's elegant standards.
translations.idiomatic: If they pass, younger men will imitate them and corrupt Your Majesty's literary standards."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，翠微宮成，獻頌闕下，召見，試《息兵詔》，少選成文。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan, when the Cuiwei Palace was completed, he presented a hymn at the palace gate, was summoned and tested with the 'Edict on Ceasing Arms'—in a short while the text was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenguan, when the Cuiwei Palace was completed, he presented a hymn at court, was summoned, and asked to draft an Edict on Ceasing Arms, which he finished in a short while.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，戒之曰：「昔禰衡、潘嶽矜己慠物，不得死。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and admonished him: 'In former days Mi Heng and Pan Yue prided themselves on talent and were arrogant toward others—they did not die natural deaths.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and warned him, "Long ago Mi Heng and Pan Yue prided themselves on talent and looked down on others—they did not die natural deaths."

sentences.zh: 卿才不減二人，宜鑒於前，副朕所求。

translations.literal: Your talent is not less than those two; you should take warning from the past and fulfill what I seek.
translations.idiomatic: Your talent is no less than theirs. Take warning from the past and live up to what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕於通事舍人裏供奉。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to serve in attendance within the Retinue of the Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to serve in attendance among the masters of communications.

sentences.zh: 俄為昆山道記室，《平龜茲露布》為士所稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was Recorder on the Kunshan campaign; his 'Victory Bulletin on Pacifying Kucha' was praised by officers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as recorder on the Kunshan campaign, and his Victory Bulletin on Pacifying Kucha won praise from the officers.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭敏之奏豫北門修撰，卒。

translations.literal: He Lulan Minzhi memorialized to have him made Compiler at the North Gate of Yuzhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He Lulan Minzhi memorialized to have him made compiler at the North Gate of Yuzhou, and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 昌宗官至太子舍人、修文館學士。

translations.literal: Changzong reached the posts of Attendant to the Crown Prince and Academician of the Hall of Cultivating Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong rose to attendant to the crown prince and academician of the Hall of Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 撰《古文紀年新傳》數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored several tens of chapters of the 'New Chronicle of Ancient Texts by Year.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several dozen chapters of the New Chronicle of Ancient Texts by Year.

sentences.zh: 崔行功崔行功，恒州井陘人。

translations.literal: Cui Xinggong—Cui Xinggong was a native of Jingxing in Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinggong was a native of Jingxing in Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖謙之，仕北齊，終钜鹿太守，徙占鹿泉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianzhi served Northern Qi, ended as Prefect of Julu, and moved to settle at Luquan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianzhi served Northern Qi and ended as prefect of Julu, then moved his household to Luquan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，唐儉愛其才，妻以女，因倩作文奏。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; Tang Jian admired his talent, gave him his daughter in marriage, and had him draft memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning. Tang Jian admired his talent, gave him his daughter in marriage, and had him draft memorials.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，累轉吏部郎中，以善占奏，常兼通事舍人內供奉。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he was repeatedly transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel; because he was skilled at drafting memorials, he often concurrently served as Attendant Master of Communications in inner attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he rose to director in the Ministry of Personnel. Skilled at drafting memorials, he often served concurrently as master of communications in inner attendance.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶游安令，又召為司文郎中，與蘭台侍郎李懷儼並主朝廷大典冊。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Magistrate of You'an; he was again summoned as Director of the Bureau of Documents and, with Lantai Vice Director Li Huaiyan, jointly oversaw the court's great ordinances and registers.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to magistrate of You'an, then recalled as director of the Bureau of Documents. With Lantai vice director Li Huaiyan he oversaw the court's great ordinances and registers.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗命秘書監魏征寫四部群書，將藏內府，置讎正三十員、書工百員。

translations.literal: At first Taizong ordered Director of the Imperial Library Wei Zheng to copy the books of the four categories to be stored in the inner palace, establishing thirty collators and a hundred copyists.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Taizong ordered Wei Zheng, director of the Imperial Library, to copy the books of the four categories for the inner palace, with thirty collators and a hundred copyists.

sentences.zh: 征徙職，又詔虞世南、顏師古踵領，功不就。

translations.literal: When Zheng was transferred, an edict again ordered Yu Shinan and Yan Shigu to succeed in leading it, but the work was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was transferred, Yu Shinan and Yan Shigu were ordered to continue the work, but it remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，罷讎正員，聽書工寫於家，送官取直，使散官隨番刊正。

translations.literal: In Xianqing, collator posts were abolished; copyists were allowed to write at home and deliver to the office for payment, with unsalaried officials taking turns in collation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing the collator posts were abolished; copyists were allowed to work at home and deliver copies to the office for payment, while unsalaried officials took turns collating.

sentences.zh: 至是詔東台侍郎趙仁本、舍人張文瓘及行功、懷儼相次充使檢校，置詳正學士代散官。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered Eastern Terrace Vice Director Zhao Renben, Attendant Zhang Wenjin, and Xinggong and Huaiyan in succession to serve as commissioners for inspection, establishing Detailed Collator Academicians to replace unsalaried officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then named Zhao Renben, Zhang Wenjin, Xinggong, and Huaiyan in succession as commissioners to supervise the project and established detailed collator academicians to replace the unsalaried officials.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷蘭台侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: For his labor he was transferred to Lantai Vice Director and died.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made Lantai vice director and died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫 銑孫銑，尚定安公主，為太府卿。

translations.literal: Grandson Xian—Xian married Princess Ding'an and was Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xian married Princess Ding'an and served as minister of the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 初，主降王同皎，後降銑，主卒，皎子繇請與父合葬。

translations.literal: At first the princess had married Wang Tongjiao; later she married Xian; when the princess died, Jiao's son You requested joint burial with his father.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had first married Wang Tongjiao and later married Xian. When she died, Jiao's son You asked that she be buried with his father.

sentences.zh: 給事中夏侯銛駁奏「主與王氏絕，喪當還崔」，詔可。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xiahou Qian memorialized in rebuttal: 'The princess severed ties with the Wang clan; the funeral should return to the Cui,' and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xiahou Qian objected that the princess had severed ties with the Wang clan and that the funeral should return to the Cui family. An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 銛猶出為瀘州都督。

translations.literal: Xian was still sent out as Military Commissioner of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was nevertheless sent out as military commissioner of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 行功兄子玄、暐別有傳。

translations.literal: Xinggong's elder brother's sons Xuan and Wei have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong's nephews Xuan and Wei have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 杜審言杜審言，字必簡，襄州襄陽人，晉征南將軍預遠裔。

translations.literal: Du Shenyan—Du Shenyan, style Bojian, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture, a distant descendant of Jin's General Who Conquers the South, Du Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenyan, style Bojian, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture and a distant descendant of the Jin general Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，為隰城尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 恃才高，以傲世見疾。

translations.literal: Relying on his lofty talent, he was resented for arrogance toward the world.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his talent, he was resented for his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 蘇味道為天官侍郎，審言集判，出謂人曰：「味道必死。

translations.literal: Su Weidao was Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments; Shenyan attended a session of judgments and, on leaving, said to people: 'Weidao will surely die.'
translations.idiomatic: When Su Weidao was vice director of the Bureau of Appointments, Shenyan attended a session of judgments and, on leaving, said, "Weidao will surely die."

sentences.zh: 」人驚問故，答曰：「彼見吾判，且羞死。

translations.literal: People were startled and asked the reason; he replied: 'When he sees my judgments, he will die of shame.'
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, he said, "When he sees my judgments, he will die of shame."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗語人曰：「吾文章當得屈、宋作衙官，吾筆當得王羲之北面。

translations.literal: He also once said to people: 'My writing ought to have Qu Yuan and Song Yu as yamen officers; my brush ought to have Wang Xizhi facing north in respect.'
translations.idiomatic: He also once said, "My writing ought to have Qu Yuan and Song Yu as my assistants; my brush ought to have Wang Xizhi bowing north before me."

sentences.zh: 」其矜誕類此。

translations.literal: His arrogant extravagance was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His boastfulness was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 累遷洛陽丞，坐事貶吉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Luoyang; for an offense he was demoted to Revenue Assistant of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant magistrate of Luoyang, then was demoted for an offense to revenue assistant of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 司馬周季重、司戶郭若訥構其罪，繫獄，將殺之。

translations.literal: Military Assistant Zhou Jizhong and Revenue Officer Guo Ruone framed his crime; he was imprisoned and about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Military assistant Zhou Jizhong and revenue officer Guo Ruone framed him, had him imprisoned, and were about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 季重等酒酣，審言子並年十三，袖刃刺季重於坐，左右殺並。

translations.literal: When Jizhong and the others were deep in wine, Shenyan's son Bing, aged thirteen, drew a blade from his sleeve and stabbed Jizhong in his seat; attendants killed Bing.
translations.idiomatic: While Jizhong and the others were deep in wine, Shenyan's thirteen-year-old son Bing drew a blade and stabbed Jizhong where he sat. Attendants killed Bing on the spot.

sentences.zh: 季重將死，曰：「審言有孝子，吾不知，若訥故誤我。

translations.literal: As Jizhong was dying he said: 'Shenyan has a filial son—I did not know; Ruone deliberately misled me.'
translations.idiomatic: As Jizhong lay dying he said, "Shenyan has a filial son—I did not know. Ruone deliberately misled me."

sentences.zh: 」審言免官，還東都。

translations.literal: Shenyan was dismissed from office and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan was dismissed from office and returned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 蘇頲傷並孝烈，志其墓，劉允濟祭以文。

translations.literal: Su Ting mourned Bing's filial heroism, wrote an inscription for his tomb, and Liu Yunji offered a funeral text.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting mourned Bing's filial courage, wrote an inscription for his tomb, and Liu Yunji offered a funeral text.

sentences.zh: 後武后召審言，將用之，問曰：「卿喜否？

translations.literal: Later Empress Wu summoned Shenyan, intending to employ him, and asked: 'Are you pleased?'
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Wu summoned Shenyan to employ him and asked, "Are you pleased?"

sentences.zh: 」審言蹈舞謝，後令賦《歡喜詩》，歎重其文，授著作佐郎，遷膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: Shenyan danced in thanks; later she ordered a 'Poem of Joy'; she sighed in admiration of his writing and appointed him Assistant Author, then transferred him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan danced in thanks. She then ordered a poem of joy, admired his writing, appointed him assistant author, and later made him vice director in the Ministry of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，坐交通張易之，流峰州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, for associating with Zhang Yizhi he was exiled to Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong he was exiled to Feng Prefecture for associating with Zhang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監主簿、修文館直學士，卒。

translations.literal: He entered service as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Education and Direct Academician of the Hall of Cultivating Literature, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as chief clerk of the Directorate of Education and direct academician of the Hall of Cultivating Literature, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 大學士李嶠等奏請加贈，詔贈著作郎。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Li Jiao and others memorialized requesting additional posthumous honors; an edict posthumously made him Author.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Li Jiao and others asked that he be honored further posthumously, and an edict made him author.

sentences.zh: 初，審言病甚，宋之問、武平一等省候何如，答曰「甚為造化小兒相苦，尚何言？

translations.literal: At first, when Shenyan was gravely ill, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, and others visited to inquire how he was; he replied: 'I am greatly tormented by the little child of creation—what more is there to say?'
translations.idiomatic: When Shenyan lay gravely ill, Song Zhiwen, Wu Pingyi, and others came to inquire after him. He said, "Creation's little imps torment me sorely—what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 然吾在，久壓公等，今且死，固大慰，但恨不見替人」云。

translations.literal: Yet while I have lived, I have long kept you gentlemen down; now that I am about to die, that is indeed great consolation—only I regret not seeing my replacements.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet while I lived I long kept you down. Now that I am dying, that is consolation enough—only I regret that I shall not see who takes my place."

sentences.zh: 少與李嶠、崔融、蘇味道為文章四友，世號「崔、李、蘇、杜」。

translations.literal: In youth he with Li Jiao, Cui Rong, and Su Weidao were the Four Friends of Literature; the age called them 'Cui, Li, Su, and Du.'
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Li Jiao, Cui Rong, and Su Weidao were known as the Four Friends of Literature, called in their day "Cui, Li, Su, and Du."

sentences.zh: 融之亡，審言為服緦云。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shenyan wore the three-month mourning for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Shenyan wore mourning for him as for a close friend.

sentences.zh: 從祖兄 易簡從祖兄易簡，九歲能屬文，長博學，為岑文本所器。

translations.literal: Cousin Yijian—Shenyan's cousin Yijian at nine could compose writing; grown, he was broadly learned and was valued by Cen Textian.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yijian could compose at nine, grew broadly learned, and was valued by Cen Textian.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，補渭南尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，曆殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng he served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianheng he served as attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗道遇吏部尚書李敬玄，不避，敬玄恨，召為考功員外郎屈之。

translations.literal: Once on the road he met Minister of Personnel Li Jingxuan and did not yield; Jingxuan resented this and summoned him as Vice Director of the Examination Section to humble him.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he met Minister of Personnel Li Jingxuan and did not step aside. Jingxuan resented this and summoned him to the Examination Section to humble him.

sentences.zh: 而侍郎裴行儉與敬玄不平，故易簡上書言敬玄罪，敬玄曰：「襄陽兒輕薄乃爾。

translations.literal: But Vice Director Pei Xingjian was on bad terms with Jingxuan, so Yijian submitted a memorial stating Jingxuan's crimes; Jingxuan said: 'This boy from Xiangyang is so frivolous.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Pei Xingjian was on bad terms with Jingxuan, so Yijian memorialized against him. Jingxuan said, "This boy from Xiangyang is insufferably frivolous."

sentences.zh: 」因奏易簡險躁，高宗怒，貶開州司馬。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that Yijian was dangerous and rash; Gaozong was angry and demoted him to Military Assistant of Kai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then accused Yijian of being dangerous and rash. Gaozong was angry and demoted him to military assistant of Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孫 甫審言生子閑，閑生甫。

translations.literal: Grandson Fu—Shenyan's son was Xian, and Xian begot Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Fu was born to Shenyan's son Xian.

sentences.zh: 甫，字子美，少貧不自振，客吳越、齊趙間。

translations.literal: Fu, style Zimei, in youth was poor and could not lift himself up; he traveled as a guest among Wu-Yue and Qi-Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, style Zimei, was poor in youth and could not establish himself. He wandered as a guest through Wu-Yue and Qi-Zhao.

sentences.zh: 李邕奇其材，先往見之。

translations.literal: Li Yong marveled at his talent and went first to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong admired his talent and went to visit him first.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不中第，困長安。

translations.literal: He entered the jinshi examination but failed; he was stranded in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination and remained stranded in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，玄宗朝獻太清宮，饗廟及郊，甫奏賦三篇。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, Xuanzong offered sacrifice at the Grand Pure Palace, feasted at the ancestral temple, and sacrificed at the suburban altar; Fu presented three rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, when Xuanzong sacrificed at the Grand Pure Palace, the ancestral temple, and the suburban altar, Fu presented three rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，使待制集賢院，命宰相試文章，擢河西尉，不拜，改右衛率府胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at them, had him await appointment at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, ordered the chief ministers to test his writing, promoted him to Assistant Magistrate of Hexi—he did not accept—and changed him to Military Staff Officer in the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired them, had him await appointment at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and ordered the chief ministers to test his writing. He was promoted to assistant magistrate of Hexi but declined, and was made military staff officer in the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 數上賦頌，因高自稱道，且言：「先臣恕、預以來，承儒守官十一世，迨審言，以文章顯中宗時。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted rhapsodies and hymns, and thereby praised himself highly, saying: 'From former ministers Shu and Yu onward, for eleven generations we have inherited Confucian learning and held office; down to Shenyan, who was illustrious through literature in Zhongzong's time.'
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted rhapsodies and hymns and spoke highly of himself, saying, "From my ancestors Shu and Yu, for eleven generations our house has inherited learning and held office. Down to Shenyan, we won fame through writing under Zhongzong."

sentences.zh: 臣賴緒業，自七歲屬辭，且四十年，然衣不蓋體，常寄食於人，竊恐轉死溝壑，伏惟天子哀憐之。

translations.literal: Your servant relies on this inherited work; from age seven I have composed, and it is already forty years, yet my clothes do not cover my body and I often depend on others for food; I fear in secret I may die in ditches and gullies—may Your Majesty pity me.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on this inheritance. I have written since I was seven, and it has been forty years, yet my clothes barely cover me and I often depend on others for food. I fear I may die in a ditch—may Your Majesty pity me."

sentences.zh: 若令執先臣故事，拔泥塗之久辱，則臣之述作雖不足鼓吹《六經》，至沈郁頓挫，隨時敏給，揚雄、枚皋可企及也。

translations.literal: If you order me to follow my forebears' precedent and lift me from long disgrace in the mire, then though my compositions are not enough to exalt the Six Classics, in depth, restraint, and timely readiness I may approach Yang Xiong and Mei Gao.
translations.idiomatic: If you raise me from long disgrace in the mire as you did my forebears, my writing may not exalt the Six Classics, yet in depth, restraint, and timely power I may approach Yang Xiong and Mei Gao."

sentences.zh: 有臣如此，陛下其忍棄之？

translations.literal: With a minister such as this, can Your Majesty bear to abandon him?
translations.idiomatic: With a minister such as I, can Your Majesty bear to abandon me?"

sentences.zh: 會祿山亂，天子入蜀，甫避走三川。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, the Son of Heaven entered Shu; Fu fled to the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, the emperor fled to Shu, and Fu escaped to the Three Rivers region.
