sentences.zh: 肅宗立，自鄜州羸服欲奔行在，為賊所得。

translations.literal: When Suzong was established, from Fuzhou in worn clothes he wished to rush to the imperial camp and was captured by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was enthroned, Fu set out from Fuzhou in travel-worn clothes to reach the imperial camp and was captured by rebels.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，亡走鳳翔上謁，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he escaped to Fengxiang and presented himself, and was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide he escaped to Fengxiang and was appointed right reminder.

sentences.zh: 與房琯為布衣交，琯時敗陳濤斜，又以客董廷蘭，罷宰相。

translations.literal: He and Fang Guan were friends as commoners; Guan had then been defeated at Taoxie, and again because of his guest Dong Tinglan was dismissed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fang Guan had been friends in common life. Guan was then defeated at Chen-Taoxie and, because of his guest Dong Tinglan, was dismissed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 甫上疏言：「罪細，不宜免大臣。

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying: 'The offense is slight; it is not fitting to dismiss a great minister.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized, "The offense is slight. It is not fitting to dismiss a great minister."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，詔三司親問。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered the Three Offices to question him in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered the Three Offices to question him in person.

sentences.zh: 宰相張鎬曰：「甫若抵罪，絕言者路。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Gao said: 'If Fu is punished, the road of those who speak will be cut off.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Gao said, "If Fu is punished, the path of frank counsel will be cut off."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then released him.

sentences.zh: 甫謝，且稱：「琯宰相子，少自樹立為醇儒，有大臣體，時論許琯才堪公輔，陛下果委而相之。

translations.literal: Fu thanked him and also said: 'Guan is a chancellor's son who from youth established himself as a pure Confucian, with the bearing of a great minister; public opinion held Guan's talent fit for chief minister, and Your Majesty indeed entrusted and made him chancellor.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu thanked him and said, "Guan is a chancellor's son who from youth made himself a pure scholar with the bearing of a great minister. Public opinion held him fit for high office, and Your Majesty indeed made him chancellor."

sentences.zh: 觀其深念主憂，義形於色，然性失于簡。

translations.literal: Observing him, he deeply thought on the ruler's worries and righteousness showed in his countenance, yet his nature failed in simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply shared the ruler's cares and showed it in his face, yet his nature lacked restraint.

sentences.zh: 酷嗜鼓琴，廷蘭托琯門下，貧疾昏老，依倚為非，琯愛惜人情，一至玷污。

translations.literal: He was passionately fond of the zither; Tinglan relied on Guan's patronage—poor, ill, dim-eyed and old—and leaned on him for wrongdoing; Guan cherished human feeling to the point of being stained.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the zither passionately. Tinglan relied on Guan's patronage—poor, ill, and old—and used it for wrong ends. Guan cherished personal ties to the point of being stained.

sentences.zh: 臣歎其功名未就，志氣挫衄，覬陛下棄細錄大，所以冒死稱述，涉近訐激，違忤聖心。

translations.literal: Your servant sighed that his merit and fame were not yet achieved and his will was broken; hoping Your Majesty would discard the small and record the great, I therefore risked death to state this, approaching slander and provocation and going against the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: I grieved that his merit was unfinished and his spirit broken, and hoped Your Majesty would overlook small faults and value great service. Therefore I risked death to speak, though it bordered on offense and went against Your Majesty's will.

sentences.zh: 陛下赦臣百死，再賜骸骨，天下之幸，非臣獨蒙。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pardoned your servant a hundred deaths and again granted my bones—this is the fortune of the realm, not mine alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pardoned me when I deserved death a hundred times and granted me life again. That is the realm's fortune, not mine alone."

sentences.zh: 」然帝自是不甚省錄。

translations.literal: Yet from then on the Emperor did not greatly attend to or employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from then on the emperor paid him little attention.

sentences.zh: 時所在寇奪，甫家寓鄜，彌年艱窶，孺弱至餓死，因許甫自往省視。

translations.literal: At the time bandits plundered everywhere; Fu's family lodged in Fu Prefecture, year after year in hardship and want, the young even starving to death; he was therefore permitted to go himself to visit them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ravaged the land. Fu's family lodged in Fu Prefecture, year after year in want, until the young starved to death. He was permitted to go visit them himself.

sentences.zh: 從還京師，出為華州司功參軍。

translations.literal: Returning with him to the capital, he was sent out as Revenue Assistant of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he was sent out as revenue assistant of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 關輔饑，輒棄官去，客秦州，負薪采橡栗自給。

translations.literal: Guanzhong suffered famine; he promptly abandoned office and left, lodging in Qin Prefecture, carrying firewood and gathering acorns to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong suffered famine, he abandoned office and lodged in Qin Prefecture, gathering firewood and acorns to live.

sentences.zh: 流落劍南，結廬成都西郭。

translations.literal: He drifted to Jiannan and built a hut west of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He drifted to Jiannan and built a hut west of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 召補京兆功曹參軍，不至。

translations.literal: He was summoned to fill the post of Merit Officer of the Capital District but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as merit officer of the capital district but did not go.

sentences.zh: 會嚴武節度劍南東、西川，往依焉。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu was military commissioner of eastern and western Jiannan, he went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu became military commissioner of eastern and western Jiannan, Fu went to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 武再帥劍南，表為參謀，檢校工部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Wu again commanded Jiannan, he memorialized Fu as staff officer and Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu again commanded Jiannan, he memorialized Fu as staff officer and acting vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 武以世舊，待甫甚善，親至其家。

translations.literal: Wu, because of old family ties, treated Fu very well and personally visited his home.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, because of old family ties, treated Fu very well and visited his home in person.

sentences.zh: 甫見之，或時不巾，而性褊躁傲誕，嘗醉登武床，瞪視曰：「嚴挺之乃有此兒！

translations.literal: When Fu saw him he sometimes wore no headcloth; his nature was narrow, rash, arrogant, and extravagant; once drunk he climbed onto Wu's couch, stared, and said: 'Yan Tingzhi actually had a son like this!'
translations.idiomatic: When Fu received him he sometimes wore no cap. Proud, irritable, and unrestrained, he once climbed drunk onto Wu's couch, stared at him, and said, "So Yan Tingzhi had a son like this!"

sentences.zh: 」武亦暴猛，外若不為忤，中銜之。

translations.literal: Wu too was fierce and violent; outwardly he seemed not offended, inwardly he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu too was fierce. Outwardly he showed no offense, but inwardly he resented it.

sentences.zh: 一日欲殺甫及梓州刺史章彝，集吏於門。

translations.literal: One day he wished to kill Fu and Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, and gathered officials at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: One day he meant to kill Fu and Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, and gathered his officers at the gate.

sentences.zh: 武將出，冠鉤於簾三，左右白其母，奔救得止，獨殺彝。

translations.literal: As Wu was about to go out, his cap caught on the curtain three times; attendants told his mother, who ran to save them and stopped it—only Yi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu was about to go out, his cap caught on the curtain three times. Attendants told his mother, who ran to stop him. Only Zhang Yi was killed.

sentences.zh: 武卒，崔旰等亂，甫往來梓、夔間。

translations.literal: When Wu died, Cui Gan and others rebelled; Fu traveled back and forth between Zi and Kui.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu died, Cui Gan and others rebelled, and Fu traveled between Zi and Kui.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，出瞿唐，下江陵，溯沅、湘以登衡山，因客耒陽。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he left Qutang, went down to Jiangling, went up the Yuan and Xiang to ascend Mount Heng, and lodged as a guest in Leiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he left Qutang, went down to Jiangling, ascended the Yuan and Xiang to Mount Heng, and lodged in Leiyang.

sentences.zh: 游岳祠，大水遽至，涉旬不得食，縣令具舟迎之，乃得還。

translations.literal: Visiting the mountain shrine, sudden flood came; for more than ten days he had no food; the magistrate prepared a boat to welcome him, and only then could he return.
translations.idiomatic: While visiting the mountain shrine, a sudden flood came. For more than ten days he had no food until the magistrate sent a boat for him.

sentences.zh: 令嘗饋牛炙白酒，大醉，一昔卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: The magistrate once presented roast beef and white wine; he drank deeply and died in one night, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate once gave him roast beef and white wine. He drank deeply and died that night, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 甫曠放不自檢，好論天下大事，高而不切。

translations.literal: Fu was unrestrained and did not restrain himself, fond of discussing great affairs of the realm—lofty but not practical.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was unrestrained and undisciplined, fond of discussing great affairs of state—lofty but impractical.

sentences.zh: 少與李白齊名，時號「李杜」。

translations.literal: In youth he was equally famous with Li Bai; the age called them 'Li and Du.'
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was as famous as Li Bai, and the age spoke of "Li and Du."

sentences.zh: 嘗從白及高適過汴州，酒酣登吹台，慷慨懷古，人莫測也。

translations.literal: He once followed Bai and Gao Shi through Bian Prefecture; when wine was deep they ascended the Terrace of the Wind and, impassioned, thought on antiquity—no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled with Li Bai and Gao Shi through Bian Prefecture. Deep in wine, they climbed the Terrace of the Wind and spoke passionately of antiquity in ways no one could fathom.

sentences.zh: 數嘗寇亂，挺節無所汙，為歌詩，傷時橈弱，情不忘君，人憐其忠云。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he experienced bandit turmoil, upheld integrity without stain, composed songs and poems lamenting the age's weakness, his feeling never forgetting the ruler—people pitied his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived through repeated rebellions, upheld his integrity unstained, and wrote poems lamenting the age's weakness while never forgetting his loyalty to the throne. People pitied his devotion.

sentences.zh: 杜甫贊贊曰：唐興，詩人承陳、隋風流，浮靡相矜。

translations.literal: Eulogy on Du Fu—Eulogy says: When Tang rose, poets inherited the lingering style of Chen and Sui, frivolous and ornate, each priding himself on the other.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy on Du Fu: When Tang rose, poets inherited the lingering Chen and Sui manner—frivolous and ornate, each priding himself on display.

sentences.zh: 至宋之問、沈佺期等，研揣聲音，浮切不差，而號「律詩」，競相襲沿。

translations.literal: Down to Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, and others, they studied and tested sounds and tones, light and sharp without error, and called it 'regulated verse,' each competing to follow along.
translations.idiomatic: By Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, and others, poets refined sound and tone into regulated verse, which all competed to imitate.

sentences.zh: 逮開元間，稍裁以雅正，然恃華者質反，好麗者壯違，人得一概，皆自名所長。

translations.literal: By the Kaiyuan era they were somewhat trimmed toward elegance and correctness, yet those who relied on ornament turned substance upside down, and those who loved beauty opposed vigor; each grasped one aspect and all named their own specialty.
translations.idiomatic: By Kaiyuan they were somewhat trimmed toward elegance, yet those who prized ornament lost substance and those who loved beauty lost force. Each seized one aspect and called it his own.

sentences.zh: 至甫，渾涵汪茫，千匯萬狀，兼古今而有之，它人不足，甫乃厭餘，殘膏賸馥，沾丐後人多矣。

translations.literal: When it came to Fu, he was vast and boundless, a thousand convergences and ten thousand forms, embracing ancient and modern together; others were not enough, while Fu had surplus; the dregs and leftover fragrance have moistened and begged from many later men.
translations.idiomatic: With Fu, poetry became vast and boundless, embracing every form ancient and modern. Others fell short while he had more than enough; the fragrance left in his wake has enriched countless later poets.

sentences.zh: 故元稹謂：「詩人以來，未有如子美者。

translations.literal: Therefore Yuan Zhen said: 'Since poets began, there has been none like Zimei.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen said, "Since poets began, there has been none like Zimei."

sentences.zh: 」甫又善陳時事，律切精深，至千言不少衰，世號「詩史」。

translations.literal: Fu was also skilled at stating affairs of the time; his regulated verse was incisive and profound, reaching a thousand words without decline—the age called him 'Poetic History.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu also excelled at recording the affairs of his time in verse of incisive depth, sustaining power even in poems of a thousand lines. The age called him Poetic History.

sentences.zh: 昌黎韓愈于文章慎許可，至歌詩，獨推曰：「李、杜文章在，光焰萬丈長。

translations.literal: Han Yu of Changli was cautious in granting approval in prose, but in song and poetry alone he praised, saying: 'The writings of Li and Du remain—their radiance ten thousand feet long.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu of Changli was sparing in praise of prose, but of poetry he said alone, "While Li and Du remain, their radiance stretches ten thousand feet."

sentences.zh: 」誠可信云。

translations.literal: This is truly credible.
translations.idiomatic: That judgment is truly credible.

sentences.zh: 王勃王勃，字子安，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Wang Bo—Wang Bo, style Zi'an, was a native of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo, style Zi'an, was a native of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六歲善文辭，九歲得顏師古注《漢書》讀之，作《指瑕》以擿其失。

translations.literal: At six he was skilled in literary composition; at nine he obtained Yan Shigu's commentary on the 'Book of Han' and read it, composing 'Pointing Out Flaws' to expose its errors.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was skilled in writing. At nine he read Yan Shigu's commentary on the Book of Han and wrote Pointing Out Flaws to expose its errors.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，劉祥道巡行關內，勃上書自陳，祥道表於朝，對策高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Linde, Liu Xiangdao toured within the passes; Bo submitted a memorial presenting himself; Xiangdao memorialized to court, and he answered the examination with high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Linde, Liu Xiangdao toured Guanzhong. Bo submitted a self-recommendation, and Liu memorialized him to court. He passed the examination with high honors.

sentences.zh: 年未及冠，授朝散郎，數獻頌闕下。

translations.literal: Before he had reached capped age he was appointed Gentleman for Dispersed Service and repeatedly presented hymns at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he was made gentleman for dispersed service and repeatedly presented hymns at court.

sentences.zh: 沛王聞其名，召署府修撰，論次《平臺秘略》。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pei heard his name and summoned him as household compiler to arrange the 'Secret Essentials of the Terrace of Peace.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pei heard of him and summoned him as household compiler to compile the Secret Essentials of the Terrace of Peace.

sentences.zh: 書成，王愛重之。

translations.literal: When the book was complete, the prince cherished it.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished, the prince valued it highly.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸王鬥雞，勃戲為文檄英王雞，高宗怒曰：「是且交構。

translations.literal: At that time the princes were cockfighting; Bo in jest composed a written proclamation for the Prince of Ying's cock; Gaozong was angry and said: 'This will sow discord.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time the princes were cockfighting. Bo jestingly wrote a proclamation for the Prince of Ying's cock. Gaozong was angry and said, "This will sow discord among them."

sentences.zh: 」斥出府。

translations.literal: He was expelled from the household.
translations.idiomatic: He was expelled from the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 勃既廢，客劍南。

translations.literal: After Bo was dismissed, he traveled as a guest in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he traveled as a guest in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 嘗登葛憒山曠望，慨然思諸葛亮之功，賦詩見情。

translations.literal: He once ascended Mount Gefen and gazed into the distance, sighing at Zhuge Liang's achievements and composing a poem to express his feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He once climbed Mount Gefen and gazed into the distance, moved by Zhuge Liang's achievements, and wrote a poem to express his feeling.

sentences.zh: 聞虢州多藥草，求補參軍。

translations.literal: Hearing that Guo Prefecture had many medicinal herbs, he sought appointment as military assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Guo Prefecture had many medicinal herbs, he sought appointment as military assistant.

sentences.zh: 倚才陵藉，為僚吏共嫉。

translations.literal: Relying on his talent he bullied others and was jointly resented by fellow officials.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his talent he bullied others, and his colleagues resented him.

sentences.zh: 官奴曹達抵罪，匿勃所，懼事泄，輒殺之。

translations.literal: The official slave Cao Da was guilty of an offense and hid at Bo's place; fearing the matter would leak out, Bo promptly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The official slave Cao Da, guilty of an offense, hid at Bo's place. Fearing exposure, Bo killed him.

sentences.zh: 事覺當誅，會赦除名。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered he should have been executed; an amnesty came and his name was struck.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was discovered he deserved execution, but an amnesty spared him and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 父福畤，繇雍州司功參軍坐勃故左遷交址令。

translations.literal: His father Fuzhi, from his post as Revenue Assistant of Yong Prefecture, because of Bo's offense was demoted and transferred to Magistrate of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fuzhi, revenue assistant of Yong Prefecture, was demoted to magistrate of Jiaozhi because of Bo's offense.

sentences.zh: 勃往省，度海溺水，痵而卒，年二十九。

translations.literal: Bo went to visit him, crossed the sea and drowned, fell ill and died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Bo went to visit him, drowned crossing the sea, fell ill, and died, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初，道出鐘陵，九月九日都督大宴滕王閣，宿命其婿作序以誇客，因出紙筆遍請客，莫敢當，至勃，沆然不辭。

translations.literal: At first, passing through Zhongling, on the ninth day of the ninth month the military commissioner held a great banquet at the Pavilion of Prince Teng, having beforehand ordered his son-in-law to compose the preface to impress the guests; he therefore produced paper and brush and asked each guest in turn—none dared accept—until Bo, who readily did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing through Zhongling on the Double Ninth, the prefect held a great banquet at the Pavilion of Prince Teng. He had already arranged for his son-in-law to write the preface to impress the guests, then offered brush and paper to each guest in turn. None dared accept until Bo, who accepted without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 都督怒，起更衣，遣吏伺其文輒報。

translations.literal: The commissioner was angry, rose to change clothes, and sent an official to watch his text and report at once.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was angry, rose to change clothes, and sent an official to report each passage as Bo wrote.

sentences.zh: 一再報，語益奇，乃矍然曰：「天才也！

translations.literal: Report after report came; the language grew ever more marvelous, and he started in alarm: 'A heavenly talent!'
translations.idiomatic: Report after report came, each more marvelous than the last. The prefect started up and cried, "A heavenly talent!"

sentences.zh: 」請遂成文，極歡罷。

translations.literal: He asked him to finish the piece; the feast ended in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Bo to finish the piece, and the feast ended in great delight.

sentences.zh: 勃屬文，初不精思，先磨墨數升，則酣飲，引被覆面臥，及寤，援筆成篇，不易一字，時人謂勃為「腹稿」。

translations.literal: When Bo composed writing, at first he did not think deeply; he first ground several sheng of ink, then drank deeply, pulled a quilt over his face and lay down; when he awoke, he took up the brush and completed the piece, not changing a word—contemporaries called Bo's compositions 'drafts in the belly.'
translations.idiomatic: When Bo wrote, he did not ponder at first. He ground several pints of ink, drank deeply, covered his face with a quilt, and slept. When he awoke, he took up the brush and finished the piece without changing a word. People called his method "belly drafts."

sentences.zh: 尤喜著書。

translations.literal: He especially loved authoring books.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved writing books.

sentences.zh: 初，祖通，隋末居白牛溪教授，門人甚眾。

translations.literal: At first his grandfather Tong, at the end of Sui dwelt at White Ox Creek as a teacher, with very many disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong taught at White Ox Creek at the end of Sui and had many disciples.

sentences.zh: 嘗起漢、魏盡晉作書百二十篇，以續古《尚書》，後亡其序，有錄無書者十篇，勃補完缺逸，定著二十五篇。

translations.literal: He once undertook from Han and Wei through Jin to compose a hundred twenty chapters to continue the ancient 'Documents,' but later the preface was lost; ten chapters had records but no text—Bo supplemented and completed the missing parts, fixing twenty-five chapters in final form.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun a hundred twenty chapters continuing the ancient Documents from Han through Jin, but the preface was later lost and ten chapters survived only in title. Bo restored the missing parts and fixed twenty-five chapters in final form.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人子不可不知醫，時長安曹元有秘術，勃從之遊，盡得其要。

translations.literal: He once said a man's son must know medicine; at the time Cao Yuan of Chang'an had secret arts, and Bo studied with him and fully obtained the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He said a son ought to know medicine. He studied with Cao Yuan of Chang'an, who had secret medical arts, and mastered the essentials.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《易》，夜夢若有告者曰：「《易》有太極，子勉思之。

translations.literal: Once reading the 'Changes,' in a night dream someone seemed to tell him: 'The Changes has the Supreme Pole—think hard on it.'
translations.idiomatic: Once while reading the Changes, he dreamed that someone told him, "The Changes has the Supreme Pole—ponder it well."

sentences.zh: 」寤而作《易發揮》數篇，至《晉卦》，會病止。

translations.literal: Awakening, he composed several chapters of 'Elaborating the Changes,' reaching the Jin hexagram, when illness came and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On waking he wrote several chapters of Elaborating the Changes, reaching the Jin hexagram, when illness stopped him.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「王者乘土王，世五十，數盡千年；

translations.literal: He also held: 'When kings ride the sovereignty of Earth, their reigns are fifty generations, their numbers exhausting a thousand years;
translations.idiomatic: He also held that when kings ride the sovereignty of Earth, their reigns last fifty generations and a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 乘金王，世四十九，數九百年；

translations.literal: riding Metal, forty-nine generations, nine hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: riding Metal, forty-nine generations and nine hundred years;

sentences.zh: 乘水王，世二十，數六百年；

translations.literal: riding Water, twenty generations, six hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: riding Water, twenty generations and six hundred years;

sentences.zh: 乘木王，世三十，數八百年；

translations.literal: riding Wood, thirty generations, eight hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: riding Wood, thirty generations and eight hundred years;

sentences.zh: 乘火王，世二十，數七百年。

translations.literal: riding Fire, twenty generations, seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: riding Fire, twenty generations and seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: 天地之常也。

translations.literal: This is the constant of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the constant pattern of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 自黃帝至漢，五運適周，土復歸唐，唐應繼周、漢，不可承周、隋短祚。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor to Han, the Five Cycles reached completion at Zhou; Earth returned to Tang; Tang ought to succeed Zhou and Han and could not inherit the short fates of Northern Zhou and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor to Han, the Five Phases completed their cycle at Zhou. Earth returned to Tang, which ought to succeed Zhou and Han and could not inherit the brief reigns of Northern Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 」乃斥魏、晉以降非真主正統，皆五行沴氣。

translations.literal: He therefore rejected Wei, Jin, and thereafter as not true rulers of legitimate succession—all were perverse qi of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore rejected Wei, Jin, and all later dynasties as illegitimate—mere perverse emanations of the Five Phases."

sentences.zh: 遂作《唐家千歲曆》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed "The Tang House Thousand-Year Calendar."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote The Tang House Thousand-Year Calendar.

sentences.zh: 武后時，李嗣真請以周、漢為二王后，而廢周、隋，中宗復用周、隋。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, Li Sizhen requested taking Zhou and Han as the two kingly houses while abolishing Northern Zhou and Sui; Zhongzong restored Northern Zhou and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Li Sizhen asked that Zhou and Han be honored as the two kingly houses and Northern Zhou and Sui set aside; Zhongzong later restored Northern Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，太平久，上言者多以詭異進，有崔昌者采勃舊說，上《五行應運曆》，請承周、漢，廢周、隋為閏，右相李林甫亦贊佑之。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, peace had long endured; those who memorialized the throne often advanced by strange and uncanny doctrines. There was one Cui Chang who adopted Bo's old views, submitted "Calendar of the Five Phases Responding to Fortune," and asked to succeed Zhou and Han and treat Northern Zhou and Sui as intercalary lines. The Right Chancellor Li Linfu also supported him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, after long peace, memorialists often won favor with occult theories. Cui Chang took up Bo's old doctrine and submitted A Calendar of the Five Phases and Responsive Fortune, urging that Tang succeed Zhou and Han and relegate Northern Zhou and Sui to intercalary status. Right Chancellor Li Linfu backed him as well.

sentences.zh: 集公卿議可否，集賢學士衛包、起居舍人閻伯璵上表曰：「都堂集議之夕，四星聚于尾，天意昭然矣。

translations.literal: He gathered dukes and ministers to debate whether to accept it. The Hanlin scholar Wei Bao and the diary attendant Yan Bowei submitted a memorial saying: "On the evening of the assembly at the Hall, four stars gathered in Wei—the intent of Heaven is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened the chief ministers to debate the proposal. Hanlin scholar Wei Bao and diary attendant Yan Bowei memorialized: "On the night of the assembly at the chief hall, four stars gathered in the Tail constellation—Heaven's intent could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 」於是玄宗下詔以唐承漢，黜隋以前帝王，廢介、酅公，尊周、漢為二王后，以商為三恪，京城起周武王、漢高祖廟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuanzong issued an edict that Tang succeeded Han, demoted emperors before Sui, abolished the Dukes of Jie and Xi, honored Zhou and Han as the two kingly houses, took Shang as one of the three honored lineages, and built temples to King Wu of Zhou and Gaozu of Han in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong then decreed that Tang succeeded Han, demoted rulers before Sui, abolished the fiefs of the Dukes of Jie and Xi, honored Zhou and Han as the two kingly houses, ranked Shang among the three honored lineages, and erected temples to King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Gaozu of Han in the capital.

sentences.zh: 授崔昌太子贊善大夫，衛包司虞員外郎。

translations.literal: Cui Chang was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent; Wei Bao was made Vice Director in the Directorate of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chang was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and Wei Bao Vice Director in the Directorate of Parks.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠為右相，自稱隋宗，建議復用魏為三恪，周、隋為二王后，酅、介二公復舊封，貶崔昌烏雷尉，衛包夜郎尉，閻伯璵涪川尉。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong as Right Chancellor, calling himself of Sui lineage, proposed restoring Wei as one of the three honored lineages and Northern Zhou and Sui as the two kingly houses, restoring the former fiefs of the Dukes of Xi and Jie, and demoting Cui Chang to warden of Wulei, Wei Bao to warden of Yelang, and Yan Bowei to warden of Fuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong became Right Chancellor, claiming descent from the Sui house, he urged that Wei be restored among the three honored lineages and Northern Zhou and Sui as the two kingly houses, that the Dukes of Xi and Jie recover their old fiefs, and that Cui Chang be demoted to warden of Wulei, Wei Bao to warden of Yelang, and Yan Bowei to warden of Fuchuan.

sentences.zh: 勃兄勮，弟助，皆第進士。

translations.literal: Bo's elder brother Jiong and younger brother Zhu both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's elder brother Jiong and younger brother Zhu both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 兄 勮勮，長壽中為鳳閣舍人，壽春等五王出閣，有司具儀，忘載冊文，群臣已在，乃寤其闕，宰相失色。

translations.literal: Elder brother Jiong—in the Changshou era served as Fengge Attendant. When the five princes including Shouchun left the palace establishment, the offices prepared the ritual but forgot the investiture text; the ministers were already assembled when they realized the omission, and the chancellor turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jiong served as Fengge Attendant during the Changshou era. When the five princes, including Shouchun, left the palace establishment, the ritual offices prepared everything but forgot the investiture text. The ministers were already in place before anyone noticed the lapse, and the chancellor went pale.

sentences.zh: 勮召五吏執筆，分占其辭，粲然皆畢，人人嗟服。

translations.literal: Jiong summoned five clerks with brushes, divided the wording among them, and all was brilliantly completed at once—everyone sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong summoned five clerks with brushes, divided the text among them, and finished the whole document on the spot to universal admiration.

sentences.zh: 尋加弘文館學士，兼知天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as a Hanlin Academy scholar and concurrently Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a Hanlin Academy scholar and concurrently Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 始，裴行儉典選，見勮與蘇味道，曰：「二子者，皆銓衡才。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pei Xingjian supervised selection, he saw Jiong and Su Weidao and said: "Both these men have talent for the scales of office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pei Xingjian oversaw appointments, he saw Jiong and Su Weidao and said, "Both of these men have the talent to weigh offices.

sentences.zh: 」至是語驗。

translations.literal: " At this his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: " By then his words had come true.

sentences.zh: 勮素善劉思禮，用為箕州刺史，與綦連耀謀反，勮與兄涇州刺史勔及助皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Jiong had long been close to Liu Silu and appointed him governor of Ji; he plotted rebellion with Qi Lianyao. Jiong, his brother Bin governor of Jing, and Zhu were all executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had long favored Liu Silu and made him governor of Ji. Liu joined Qi Lianyao in a plot to rebel, and Jiong, his brother Bin—governor of Jing—and Zhu were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，詔復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, an edict restored their offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong era, an edict restored their offices.

sentences.zh: 弟 助助，字子功，七歲喪母哀號，鄰里為泣。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhu, styled Zigong—at seven he lost his mother and wailed in grief until the neighbors wept.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu, styled Zigong, lost his mother at seven and wailed so bitterly that the neighbors wept with him.

sentences.zh: 居父憂，毀骨立。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he wasted away until only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father he wasted away to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 服除，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served as acting Investigative Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as acting Investigative Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，勔、勮、勃皆著才名，故杜易簡稱「三珠樹」，其後助、劼又以文顯。

translations.literal: At first Bin, Jiong, and Bo were all famed for talent, so Du Yijian called them "the three pearl trees"; later Zhu and Jie also rose to notice by their writing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Bin, Jiong, and Bo were all famed for talent, and Du Yijian called them "the three pearl trees." Later Zhu and Jie also won renown through literature.

sentences.zh: 劼早卒。

translations.literal: Jie died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jie died young.

sentences.zh: 福畤少子勸亦有文。

translations.literal: Fuchuo's youngest son Quan also had literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchuo's youngest son Quan was also gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 福畤嘗詫韓思彥，思彥戲曰：「武子有馬癖，君有譽兒癖，王家癖何多耶？

translations.literal: Fuchuo once boasted to Han Siyan; Siyan jested: "Wuzi had his horse obsession—your lordship has your praise-of-sons obsession. How many obsessions in the Wang house?
translations.idiomatic: Fuchuo once boasted to Han Siyan, who jested, "Wuzi had his obsession with horses, and you have your obsession with praising sons. How many obsessions does the Wang house have?

sentences.zh: 」使助出其文，思彥曰：「生子若是，可誇也。

translations.literal: " He had Zhu bring out his writings; Siyan said: "A son like this is something to boast of.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Zhu bring out his writings. Siyan said, "A son like this is worth boasting of.

sentences.zh: 勃與楊炯、盧照鄰、駱賓王皆以文章齊名，天下稱「王、楊、盧、駱」四傑。

translations.literal: Bo with Yang Jiong, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were all equally famed for literature; the world called them the Four Talents "Wang, Yang, Lu, Luo."
translations.idiomatic: Bo, Yang Jiong, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were equally famed for their writing, and the world called them the Four Talents: Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo.

sentences.zh: 炯嘗曰：「吾愧在盧前，恥居王後。

translations.literal: Jiong once said: "I am ashamed to rank before Lu, and it shames me to rank after Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong once said, "I am ashamed to stand before Lu, and it shames me to stand after Wang.

sentences.zh: 」議者謂然。

translations.literal: " Critics agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Critics agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 附 楊炯炯，華陰人。

translations.literal: Appended: Yang Jiong, of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Yang Jiong, a native of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 舉神童，授校書郎。

translations.literal: Selected as a child prodigy, he was appointed collation officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as a child prodigy, he was appointed collation officer.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，皇太子已釋奠，表豪俊充崇文館學士，中書侍郎薛元超薦炯及鄭祖玄、鄧玄挺、崔融等，詔可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, after the crown prince had performed the capping sacrifice, he memorialized that eminent talents fill Chongwen Hall. The Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao recommended Jiong together with Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xuanbing, Cui Rong, and others—the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonglong, after the crown prince's capping sacrifice, he memorialized that outstanding men be appointed Chongwen Hall scholars. Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao recommended Jiong along with Zheng Zuxuan, Deng Xuanbing, Cui Rong, and others, and the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 遷詹事司直。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Clerk in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Clerk in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 俄坐從父弟神讓與徐敬業亂，出為梓州司法參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was implicated because his cousin Shen Rang joined Xu Jingye's rebellion and was sent out as judicial aide in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was implicated when his cousin Shen Rang joined Xu Jingye's rebellion and was sent out as judicial aide in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷盈川令，張說以箴贈行，戒其苛。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Yingchuan; Zhang Yue gave him an admonition on departure, warning against harshness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Yingchuan. Zhang Yue sent him off with a written admonition warning him against harsh rule.

sentences.zh: 至官，果以嚴酷稱，吏稍忤意，搒殺之，不為人所多。

translations.literal: On reaching office he was indeed known for severity; when clerks slightly displeased him he beat them to death—winning little esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In office he lived up to his reputation for severity: when a clerk slightly displeased him, he had him beaten to death, and he won little esteem.

sentences.zh: 卒官下，中宗時贈著作郎。

translations.literal: He died in office; under Zhongzong he was posthumously made Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Compiler under Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 附 盧照鄰照鄰，字昇之，范陽人。

translations.literal: Appended: Lu Zhaolin, styled Shengzhi, of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Lu Zhaolin, styled Shengzhi, a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 十歲從曹憲、王義方授《蒼》、《雅》。

translations.literal: At ten he studied the Cangjie and Erya lexicons under Cao Xian and Wang Yifang.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he studied the Cangjie and Erya lexicons under Cao Xian and Wang Yifang.

sentences.zh: 調鄧王府典簽，王愛重，謂人曰：「此吾之相如。

translations.literal: He was appointed record-keeper to the Prince of Deng; the prince cherished him and told others: "He is my Sima Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed record-keeper to the Prince of Deng, who cherished him and told others, "He is my Sima Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 」調新都尉，病去官，居太白山，得方士玄明膏餌之，會父喪，號嘔，丹輒出，由是疾益甚。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Xindu; illness led him to leave office. He dwelt on Mount Taibai, obtained the Daoist elixir Xuaming from a master and took it; when his father died he wailed and vomited until the pills came out, and from this his illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Xindu, but illness forced him to leave office. He lived on Mount Taibai, obtained the Daoist elixir Xuaming from a master, and took it. When his father died he wailed and vomited until the pills came out, and his illness grew worse.

sentences.zh: 客東龍門山，布衣藜羹，裴瑾之、韋方質、範履冰等時時供衣藥。

translations.literal: He lodged east at Longmen Mountain in hemp robes eating coarse gruel; Pei Jinzhi, Wei Fangzhi, Fan Lubing, and others from time to time supplied clothes and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed east of Longmen Mountain in hemp robes on coarse food, while Pei Jinzhi, Wei Fangzhi, Fan Lubing, and others from time to time supplied him with clothes and medicine.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，足攣，一手又廢，乃去具茨山下，買園數十畝，疏潁水周舍，復豫為墓，偃臥其中。

translations.literal: As his illness worsened his feet cramped and one hand was crippled; he went below Mount Juci, bought several dozen mu of garden land, channeled the Ying River around his lodge, prepared his tomb in advance, and lay within it.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened his feet cramped and one hand was crippled. He moved below Mount Juci, bought several dozen mu of land, channeled the Ying around his lodge, prepared his tomb in advance, and lay within it.

sentences.zh: 照鄰自以當高宗時尚吏，己獨儒；

translations.literal: Zhaolin felt that in Gaozong's time the court favored administrators while he alone upheld Confucian learning;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin felt that in Gaozong's time the court favored administrators while he alone upheld Confucian learning;

sentences.zh: 武后尚法，己獨黃老；

translations.literal: under Wu Hou it favored law while he alone upheld Huang-Lao;
translations.idiomatic: under Empress Wu it favored law while he alone upheld Huang-Lao doctrine;

sentences.zh: 後封嵩山，屢聘賢士，己已廢。

translations.literal: later when Feng Shan was performed and worthies were repeatedly summoned, he was already disabled.
translations.idiomatic: later, when the Feng and Shan rites were performed and worthies were repeatedly summoned, he was already crippled.

sentences.zh: 著《五悲文》以自明。

translations.literal: He wrote "Five Laments" to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Five Laments to explain his plight.

sentences.zh: 病既久，與親屬訣，自沈潁水。

translations.literal: Long ill, he took leave of his kin and drowned himself in the Ying.
translations.idiomatic: After long illness he bade his kin farewell and drowned himself in the Ying River.

sentences.zh: 附 駱賓王賓王，義烏人。

translations.literal: Appended: Luo Binwang, of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Luo Binwang, a native of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 七歲能賦詩。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose fu.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could compose fu poetry.

sentences.zh: 初為道王府屬，嘗使自言所能，賓王不答。

translations.literal: At first he served as retainer to the Prince of Dao; once told to state his abilities, Binwang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as retainer to the Prince of Dao. When asked to state his abilities, Binwang did not answer.

sentences.zh: 曆武功主簿。

translations.literal: He served successively as recorder in Gong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder in Gong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉為洮州總管，表掌書奏，不應，調長安主簿。

translations.literal: When Pei Xingjian was commandant of Tao prefecture he memorialized that Binwang handle documents; he did not accept and was transferred to recorder in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Xingjian was commandant of Tao prefecture he asked that Binwang handle his documents, but Binwang declined and was transferred to recorder in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 武后時，數上疏言事。

translations.literal: Under Wu Hou he often memorialized on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he often submitted memorials on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 下除臨海丞，鞅鞅不得志，棄官去。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant magistrate of Linhai; discontented and unfulfilled, he abandoned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to assistant magistrate of Linhai. Discontented and thwarted, he abandoned his post and left.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業亂，署賓王為府屬，為敬業傳檄天下，斥武后罪。

translations.literal: In Xu Jingye's rebellion Binwang was appointed staff member of the headquarters and drafted the manifesto sent throughout the realm condemning Wu Hou's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: During Xu Jingye's rebellion Binwang was made a staff member of his headquarters and drafted the manifesto sent throughout the realm condemning Empress Wu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 后讀，但嘻笑，至「一抔之土未乾，六尺之孤安在」，矍然曰：「誰為之？

translations.literal: The Empress read it and only chuckled until she came to "the mound of earth is not yet dry—where is the six-foot orphan?" Then she started and said: "Who wrote this?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress read it and only chuckled until she came to the line, "The mound of earth is not yet dry—where is the six-foot orphan?" Then she started and said, "Who wrote this?

sentences.zh: 」或以賓王對，后曰：「宰相安得失此人！

translations.literal: " Someone named Binwang; the Empress said: "How could the chancellor let us lose such a man!
translations.idiomatic: " Someone named Binwang. The Empress said, "How could the chancellor let us lose such a man!

sentences.zh: 」敬業敗，賓王亡命，不知所之。

translations.literal: " Jingye was defeated; Binwang fled for his life and his fate is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingye was defeated. Binwang fled for his life, and no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 中宗昌，詔求其文，得數百篇。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong restored the throne, an edict sought his writings and several hundred pieces were found.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong restored the throne, an edict sought out his writings, and several hundred pieces were recovered.

sentences.zh: 它日，崔融與張說評勃等曰：「勃文章宏放，非常人所及，炯、照鄰可以企之。

translations.literal: Another day Cui Rong and Zhang Yue evaluated Bo and the others, saying: "Bo's writing is grand and expansive, beyond what ordinary men can reach; Jiong and Zhaolin can approach him.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Cui Rong and Zhang Yue assessed Bo and the others. Cui Rong said, "Bo's writing is grand and far beyond ordinary men; Jiong and Zhaolin can approach him.

sentences.zh: 」說曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 盈川文如縣河，酌之不竭，優於盧而不減王。

translations.literal: Yingchuan's writing is like a river hung in the air—draw from it and it never runs dry; better than Lu and not less than Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan's writing is like a river hung in the sky: draw from it and it never runs dry. He surpasses Lu and is no less than Wang.

sentences.zh: 恥居後，信然；

translations.literal: Shame at ranking last—that was sincere;
translations.idiomatic: His shame at ranking last was sincere;

sentences.zh: 愧在前，謙也。

translations.literal: shame at ranking first—that was modesty.
translations.idiomatic: his shame at ranking first was modesty.

sentences.zh: 開元中，說與徐堅論近世文章，說曰：「李嶠、崔融、薛稷、宋之問之文如良金美玉，無施不可。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Yue discussed recent writing with Xu Jian and said: "The writing of Li Jiao, Cui Rong, Xue Ji, and Song Zhiwen is like fine gold and beautiful jade—there is no use to which it cannot be put.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era Zhang Yue discussed recent writing with Xu Jian and said, "The prose of Li Jiao, Cui Rong, Xue Ji, and Song Zhiwen is like fine gold and polished jade—fit for any use.

sentences.zh: 富嘉謨如孤峰絕岸，壁立萬仞，濃雲鬱興，震雷俱發，誠可畏也；

translations.literal: Fu Jiamo is like a lone peak and sheer cliff, ten thousand ren high, thick clouds darkening and rising, thunder all bursting forth—truly awe-inspiring;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jiamo's is like a lone peak and sheer cliff ten thousand ren high, thick clouds gathering and thunder breaking all at once—truly awe-inspiring;

sentences.zh: 若施於廊廟，駭矣。

translations.literal: but used in the court hall, alarming indeed.
translations.idiomatic: but used in the court hall, it would be alarming.

sentences.zh: 閻朝隱如麗服靚妝，燕歌趙舞，觀者忘疲，若類之《風》、《雅》，則罪人矣。

translations.literal: Yan Chaoyin is like splendid dress and fine makeup, Yan songs and Zhao dances—viewers forget fatigue; classified with the Airs and Odes of the Book of Poetry, he would be a criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chaoyin's is like splendid dress and fine makeup, Yan songs and Zhao dances that leave viewers forgetting fatigue; class him with the Airs and Odes and he would be guilty of presumption.

sentences.zh: 」堅問：「今世奈何？

translations.literal: " Xu Jian asked: "What of the present age?
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Jian asked, "What of writers today?

sentences.zh: 」說曰：「韓休之文如大羹玄酒，有典則，薄滋味。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Han Xiu's writing is like the great broth and dark wine—has canonical pattern, thin in flavor.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said, "Han Xiu's writing is like the great broth and dark wine: it has canonical form but little savor.

sentences.zh: 許景先如豐肌膩理，雖穠華可愛，而乏風骨。

translations.literal: Xu Jingxian is like full flesh and fine grain—though lush and lovely, lacking bone and sinew.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingxian's is like full flesh and fine grain: lush and lovely, but lacking bone and sinew.

sentences.zh: 張九齡如輕縑素練，實濟時用，而窘邊幅。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling is like light silk plain weave—truly useful for the age, but straitened in scope.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling's is like light silk on plain weave: truly useful for the times, but narrow in scope.

sentences.zh: 王翰如瓊杯玉斝，雖爛然可珍，而多玷缺。

translations.literal: Wang Han is like jade cups—though brilliantly precious, many flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han's is like jade cups: though brilliantly precious, full of flaws.

sentences.zh: 」堅謂篤論云。

translations.literal: " Xu Jian called this penetrating judgment.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Jian called this penetrating judgment.

sentences.zh: 元萬頃元萬頃，後魏京兆王子推裔。

translations.literal: Yuan Wandian—Yuan Wandian, descendant of Prince Tui of Northern Wei of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wandian was a descendant of Prince Tui of Northern Wei of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖白澤，武德中，仕至梁、利十一州都督，封新安公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bai Ze, in the Wude era, served to governor of the eleven prefectures of Liang and Li and was enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bai Ze, in the Wude era, rose to governor of eleven prefectures in Liang and Li and was enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 萬頃起家為通事舍人。

translations.literal: Wandian rose from his first office as Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wandian began his career as Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從李勣征高麗，管書記。

translations.literal: He accompanied Li Ji against Goguryeo as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Li Ji on the campaign against Goguryeo as secretary.

sentences.zh: 勣命別將郭待封以舟師赴平壤，馮師本載糧繼之，不及期。

translations.literal: Ji ordered the separate commander Guo Daifeng to take the fleet to Pyongyang; Feng Shiben carried grain in support but did not arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: Ji ordered the separate commander Guo Daifeng to take the fleet to Pyongyang, while Feng Shiben was to carry grain in support, but he failed to arrive on schedule.

sentences.zh: 欲報勣，而恐為諜所得，萬頃為作離合詩遺勣。

translations.literal: Wanting to report to Ji but fearing spies would intercept it, Wandian composed a cipher poem and sent it to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to report to Ji but fearing enemy spies, Wandian wrote him a cipher poem.

sentences.zh: 勣怒曰：「軍機切遽，何用詩為？

translations.literal: Ji angrily said: "Military affairs are urgent—what use are poems?
translations.idiomatic: Ji angrily said, "Military affairs are urgent—what use are poems?

sentences.zh: 」欲斬待封，萬頃言狀，乃免。

translations.literal: " He was about to execute Daifeng; Wandian explained the situation and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to execute Daifeng, but Wandian explained what had happened and Daifeng was spared.

sentences.zh: 又使萬頃草檄讓高麗，而譏其不知守鴨淥之險，莫離支報曰：「謹聞命。

translations.literal: Ji also had Wandian draft a proclamation rebuking Goguryeo and mocking them for not holding the crossing at the Yalu; Molizhi replied: "Your command is respectfully heard.
translations.idiomatic: Ji also had Wandian draft a proclamation rebuking Goguryeo and mocking them for failing to hold the Yalu crossing. Molizhi replied, "Your command is respectfully heard.

sentences.zh: 」徙兵固守，軍不得入。

translations.literal: " They shifted troops to stubborn defense and the army could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: " They shifted troops to stubborn defense, and the Tang army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞之，投萬頃嶺外。

translations.literal: Gaozong heard of it and banished Wandian beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong heard of it, he banished Wandian beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，為著作郎。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he returned and was made Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He returned on a general amnesty and was made Compiler.

sentences.zh: 武后諷帝召諸儒論撰禁中，萬頃與周王府戶曹參軍範履冰、苗神客、太子舍人周思茂、右史胡楚賓與選，凡撰《列女傳》、《臣軌》、《百僚新戒》、《樂書》等九千餘篇。

translations.literal: Wu Hou prompted the emperor to summon scholars for composition within the palace; Wandian with Fan Lubing, Registrar of the Prince of Zhou's household, Miao Shenke, Zhou Simao the Crown Prince's Attendant, and Hu Chubin the Right Historian were chosen. In all they compiled more than nine thousand chapters including Biographies of Exemplary Women, Mirror of Ministers, New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, Book of Music, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu urged the emperor to summon scholars to compose within the palace. Wandian was chosen together with Fan Lubing, Registrar of the Prince of Zhou's household, Miao Shenke, Crown Prince's Attendant Zhou Simao, and Right Historian Hu Chubin. Together they compiled more than nine thousand chapters, including Biographies of Exemplary Women, Mirror of Ministers, New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, and Book of Music.

sentences.zh: 至朝廷疑議表疏皆密使參處，以分宰相權，故時謂「北門學士」。

translations.literal: When the court had doubtful memorials and documents they were secretly sent to them to deliberate, splitting the chancellors' power—hence they were called "Northern Gate scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced doubtful memorials or documents, they were secretly sent to these men for deliberation, dividing the chancellors' power. Hence they were called the Northern Gate scholars.

sentences.zh: 思茂、履冰、神客供奉左右，或二十餘年。

translations.literal: Simao, Lubing, and Shenke attended at left and right, some for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Simao, Lubing, and Shenke attended at the ruler's side, some for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 萬頃敏文辭，然放達不治細檢，無儒者風。

translations.literal: Wandian was quick with words and letters, yet careless and unrestrained in small matters, without the bearing of a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Wandian was quick with words, but careless and unrestrained in small matters and lacked a scholar's bearing.

sentences.zh: 武后時，累遷鳳閣侍郎，坐誅。

translations.literal: Under Wu Hou he rose through repeated promotions to Vice Minister of Luantai and was executed for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose to Vice Minister of Luantai and was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 附 范履冰履冰者，河內人。

translations.literal: Appended: Fan Lubing—Lubing was of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Fan Lubing, a native of Henei.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，曆鸞台天官二侍郎、春官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In Chuigong he served successively as both Vice Ministers of Luantai and Tian'guan, Minister of the Spring Office, and Grand Councilor of the Tongfengge Luantai Secretariat, while also editing the state history.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he served successively as both Vice Ministers of Luantai and Tian'guan, Minister of the Spring Office, and Grand Councilor of the Tongfengge Luantai Secretariat, while also editing the state history.

sentences.zh: 載初初，坐舉逆人被殺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zai Chu he was executed for recommending rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zai Chu era he was executed for recommending rebels.

sentences.zh: 神客，東光人，終著作郎。

translations.literal: Shenke, of Dongguang, ended as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Shenke, a native of Dongguang, ended his career as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 附 周思茂思茂，漳南人，與弟思鈞早知名。

translations.literal: Appended: Zhou Simao—Simao, of Zhangnan, was early famed together with his younger brother Sijun.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zhou Simao of Zhangnan was early famed together with his younger brother Sijun.

sentences.zh: 累遷麟台少監、崇文館學士。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to Vice Director of the Lin Platform and Chongwen Hall scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Lin Platform and Chongwen Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，下獄死。

translations.literal: In Chuigong he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 附 胡楚賓楚賓，秋浦人。

translations.literal: Appended: Hu Chubin—Chubin, of Qiupu.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Hu Chubin, a native of Qiupu.

sentences.zh: 屬文敏甚，必酒中，然後下筆。

translations.literal: Extremely quick at composition—only when drunk would he set brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: He was extremely quick at composition, but would set brush to paper only when drunk.

sentences.zh: 高宗命作文，常以金銀盃畾酒飲之，文成輒賜焉。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered him to compose writing and often had him drink wine from gold and silver cups stacked high; when the text was complete he would bestow them on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong ordered him to write and often fed him wine from stacked gold and silver cups; when a piece was finished, the cups were his to keep.

sentences.zh: 家居率沈飲，無留賄，費盡復入，得賜而出，類為常。

translations.literal: At home he habitually drank deeply, kept no bribes, spent all and entered again, received gifts and went out—such was his constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: At home he drank heavily, kept no bribes, spent everything and returned for more, and left again with new gifts—a constant round.

sentences.zh: 性重慎，未嘗語禁中事，人及其醉問之，亦熟視不答。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave and cautious, never speaking of affairs within the forbidden precincts; when people questioned him even in his drunkenness, he would stare fixedly and not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and cautious by nature and never spoke of palace affairs. Even when drunk and questioned, he would stare fixedly and say nothing.

sentences.zh: 尋兼崇賢直學士，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Direct Academician of the Hall of Esteeming Worthies and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made direct academician of the Hall of Esteeming Worthies and died in office.

sentences.zh: 萬頃孫 正萬頃孫正，修名節，擢明經高第，授監門衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Wandian's grandson Zheng—Wandian's grandson Zheng cultivated integrity and reputation, passed the mingjing examination with high rank, and was appointed Military Assistant in the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Wandian's grandson Zheng cultivated integrity, passed the mingjing examination with high honors, and was appointed military assistant in the Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 舅孫逖與譚物理，歎己不逮。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle's son Sun Ti and Tan Wuli sighed that they could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Sun Ti and Tan Wuli sighed that they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，吏部尚書崔寓典選，正以書判第一召詣京師，以父詢倩老，辭疾免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong, Minister of Personnel Cui Yu presided over selection; Zheng ranked first in document judgment and was summoned to the capital, but because his father Xun was old he pleaded illness and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign, Minister of Personnel Cui Yu presided over selection. Zheng ranked first in document judgment and was summoned to the capital, but he pleaded illness to stay with his aging father Xun.

sentences.zh: 河南節度使崔光遠表置其府。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Henan Cui Guangyuan memorialized to place him in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Henan Cui Guangyuan memorialized to place him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷河、洛，輦父匿山中，賊以名購，正度事急，謂弟曰：「賊祿不可養親，彼利吾名，難免矣，然不汙身而死，吾猶生也。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming seized He and Luo, he moved his father by cart and hid him in the mountains; the rebels offered a price for his name. Zheng judged the matter urgent and told his younger brother: 'Rebel salary cannot support our parent. They covet my name—I cannot escape, yet to die without staining my person is still to live.'
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized He and Luo, he hid his father in the mountains. The rebels offered a price for his name. Seeing no escape, he told his brother, "Rebel pay cannot support our father. They want my name, and I cannot flee—but to die unstained is still to live."

sentences.zh: 」賊既得，誘以高位，瞋目固拒，兄弟皆遇害，父聞，仰藥死，路人為哭。

translations.literal: When the rebels seized him, they tempted him with high rank; he glared and firmly refused. Both brothers met disaster; when the father heard, he took poison and died, and passersby wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels seized him, they tempted him with high office, but he glared and refused. Both brothers were killed. When their father heard, he took poison and died, and passersby wept.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔錄伏節十一姓，而正為冠。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an edict recorded eleven surnames of those who upheld integrity, and Zheng stood foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, an edict recorded eleven families who upheld integrity, with Zheng's foremost.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書少監，以其子義方為華州參軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Library, and his son Yifang was made Military Aide of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice director of the Imperial Library, and his son Yifang was made military aide of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 義方義方，曆京兆府司錄，韋夏卿、李實繼為尹，事必咨之。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Yifang—Yifang served as Recorder of the Capital District; when Wei Xiaqing and Li Shi in succession became prefect, they always consulted him on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Yifang served as recorder of the capital district. When Wei Xiaqing and Li Shi became prefect in turn, each consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 曆虢商二州刺史、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Guo and Shang prefectures and Military Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Guo and Shang and as military commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 中官吐突承璀，閩人也，義方用其親屬為右職。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Tutu Chenghui was a native of Min; Yifang employed his kinsmen in high posts.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Tutu Chenghui was a native of Min, and Yifang employed his relatives in high posts.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫再當國，陰欲承璀奧助，即召義方為京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Li Jifu again held the state, he secretly wished for Chenghui's inner support and promptly summoned Yifang as Prefect of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu again held power, he secretly sought Chenghui's support and summoned Yifang as prefect of the capital.

sentences.zh: 李絳惡其黨，出為鄜坊觀察使，一切辨治，然苛刻，人多怨之。

translations.literal: Li Jiang hated his faction and sent him out as Military Commissioner of Bian and Fang; he judged and governed everything, yet was harsh, and many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang hated his faction and sent him out as military commissioner of Bian and Fang. He governed decisively but harshly, and many resented him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made regular attendant of the left.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 季方弟季方，舉明經，調楚丘尉，曆殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Jifang—Yifang's younger brother Jifang passed the mingjing examination, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Chuqiu, and served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang's younger brother Jifang passed the mingjing examination, served as assistant magistrate of Chuqiu, and rose to attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王紹表為度支員外郎，遷金、膳二部郎中，號能職。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Shao memorialized him as Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue; he was transferred to Director in the Bureaus of Revenue and Provisions and was called capable in office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Shao memorialized him as vice director in the Bureau of Revenue. He rose to director in the Bureaus of Revenue and Provisions and was known as capable in office.

sentences.zh: 王叔文用事，憚季方不為用，以兵部郎中使新羅。

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen held power, he feared Jifang would not serve him and sent him as Director in the Ministry of War on a mission to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shuwen held power, he feared Jifang would not serve him and sent him as director in the Ministry of War on a mission to Silla.

sentences.zh: 新羅聞中國喪，不時遣，供饋乏，季方正色責之，閉戶絕食待死，夷人悔謝，結歡乃還。

translations.literal: Silla heard of mourning in China and did not send envoys in season; supplies were lacking. Jifang sternly reproved them, shut his door, refused food, and awaited death; the foreigners repented and apologized, made friendship, and only then did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Silla, hearing of mourning in China, failed to send envoys on time and neglected his supplies. Jifang sternly reproved them, shut his door, and refused food until he should die. The Sillans repented, made peace, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十一，贈同州刺史。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-one, and was posthumously made Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one and was posthumously made prefect of Tong Prefecture.
